<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Eyes of the Sea](/Feats.aspx?ID=8995) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Elf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=58" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 19

**Prerequisites**
[Aquatic Elf](/Heritages.aspx?ID=435) heritage

</column>

---

Your eyes have adapted to the rigors of the sea. If you didn’t already have [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=2410), you gain darkvision. Additionally, you can see through natural phenomena that would obscure your vision underwater, such as cloudy waters, ink, smoke, and so forth, and don’t need to succeed at a [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) to target creature within these phenomena. Finally, you can cast [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) as a [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4) [innate spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=2232) once per day.

    right="Feat 18"
    pfs=""
>
[Eyes Unclouded](/Feats.aspx?ID=7341) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 116

**Archetype** [Ascended Celestial](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=289)

**Prerequisites**
[Ascended Celestial Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7331)

</column>

---

Your senses are enhanced by your divine spark, enabling you see things as they truly are, piercing through illusions, transformations, and lies. You’re affected by a constant [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) spell. Additionally, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) and to Perception DCs against attempts to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) to you. When a creature attempts to Lie to you, they roll the [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) check to Lie twice and use the worse result; this is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect.

>
[Fabricated Connections](/Feats.aspx?ID=1938) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 167

**Archetypes** [Dandy](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=55), [Venture-Gossip](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=311) (Level 7)

**Prerequisites**
[Dandy Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1935); Master in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

You can lie about having taken an action so convincingly that you acquire all the tangible benefits of having successfully completed it. You can roll [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) in place of a different skill when attempting to [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=23), [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50), [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51), or [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=27). You can use Fabricated Connections to Make an Impression or Request once per day, and you can also use it once per week to Earn Income or Subsist.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fabricated Credentials](/Feats.aspx?ID=8861) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 37

**Archetype** [Twilight Talon](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=375)

**Prerequisites**
[Twilight Talon Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8858); Master in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38)

</column>

---

You're so familiar with the paperwork necessary to maintain your cover that you can easily whip up documents that support your fabrications. You can [Create a Forgery](/Actions.aspx?ID=2402) using [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), rather than [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47), and doing so only takes 10 minutes, or 1 minute if you're legendary in Deception. With your paranoid nature, you're always on the lookout for forgeries. The GM rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=690) Perception or Society check for you any time you encounter a forgery, even if you don't examine it closely.

<title level="2">Fabricated Credentials leads to...</title>
[Instant Credentials](/Feats.aspx?ID=8866)

>
[Face Your Fears](/Feats.aspx?ID=8938) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=590" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 120

**Archetype** [Nidalese Horselord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=381)

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Nidalese Horselord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8937)

</column>

---

A lifetime of facing Nidal's terrors has taught you to fight through fear. Although you aren't immune to it, you can subdue the emotion to such an extent that many believe it doesn't affect you. Reduce the value of your [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) condition by 1. If this would reduce the value to 0, you are no longer frightened and gain a +1 circumstance bonus against fear effects for 1 minute.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fade Away](/Feats.aspx?ID=1020) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Halfling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=87" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 45

**Prerequisites**
[Easily Dismissed](/Feats.aspx?ID=1016)

</column>

---

Your ability to blend into the background allows you to fade away entirely or appear innocuous even to magical effects. You gain [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) and [_misdirection_](/Spells.aspx?ID=198) as 2nd-level innate occult spells. You can target only yourself with _invisibility_, and you must be the primary target of _misdirection_. You can cast each spell once per day.

>
[Fading](/Feats.aspx?ID=2163) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 58

**Archetype** [Red Mantis Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=17)

**Frequency**
once per Crimson Shroud

**Prerequisites**
[Crimson Shroud](/Feats.aspx?ID=898)

**Trigger**
You are targeted with a Strike by someone you can detect while your Crimson Shroud is active.

</column>

---

You fade partially from reality. The attacker must attempt a DC 11 flat check; on a failure, the attack passes harmlessly through the image of your body that remains behind. An instant later you return to reality, and your Crimson Shroud ends.

<title level="2">Secrets of the Vernai</title>

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 57

The Red Mantis Assassin archetype appears on page 71 of the _Lost Omens World Guide_. Of the additional options below, only Prayer Attack is available freely to Red Mantis assassins without prior permission from the Blood Mistress. Those who dare learn these rare abilities without her permission run the risk of being cast out of the society and hunted down by their former allies. In theory, a daring infiltration of the Crimson Citadel could allow one to study hidden texts and learn these techniques, but the chambers within and below this fortress are among the most dangerous in the region, so such an attempt should not be made lightly!

**Related Feats**: [Achaekek's Grip](/Feats.aspx?ID=2162), [Prayer Attack](/Feats.aspx?ID=2164), [Vernai Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=2165)

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Faith in the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=7759) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Claws of the Tyrant</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Claws of the Tyrant](/Sources.aspx?ID=266) pg. 113

**Archetype** [Magaambyan Attendant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=29)

**Prerequisites**
[Magaambyan Attendant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1102)

**Access**
You’re a member of the Vellumis Scholars.

</column>

---

The Gravelands are full of fallen spirits seeking to move on, and you consider it your obligation to assist in that regard. You gain the ability to store spirit wisps in your body, becoming a [_living spirit dwelling_](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=171). Each day during your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), your spirit dwelling attracts a spirit wisp who comes to dwell inside. If your _spirit dwelling_ contains no wisps, you can spend 10 minutes in a minor ritual to cast your spirit dwelling around an area and attract another wisp. Additionally, you gain a spirit wisp when a [haunt](/Traits.aspx?ID=622) or [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creature is destroyed within 30 feet of you. You gain the Spirit Sanctification action. 

**Spirit Sanctification** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513)) **Cost** 1 spirit wisp; **Effect** You immediately purify a spirit, which grants you a protective blessing before it departs. If your next action is to cast a halcyon spell, you gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws as well as [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to void damage equal to the rank of the halcyon spell. These effects last for 1 round.

Every day before your daily preparations, any spirit wisps remaining within your _spirit dwelling_ from the previous day are purified and can continue along the River of Souls.

[Faithful Steed](/Feats.aspx?ID=5885) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=811" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 94

</column>

---

You gain the service of a [young animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=2113) as a mount. If you have the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) or [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) trait, your mount gains it as well, as do the mount's Strikes. Typically, the steed is an animal companion with the mount ability (such as a [horse](/Companions.aspx?ID=76)). The GM might allow another animal companion option, or allow the creature to have a different appearance that thematically fits your deity.

<title level="2">Faithful Steed leads to...</title>
[Acclimated Mount](/Feats.aspx?ID=7991), [Faithful Stride](/Feats.aspx?ID=7992), [Heal Mount](/Feats.aspx?ID=5906), [Loyal Warhorse](/Feats.aspx?ID=5900), [Pale Horse](/Feats.aspx?ID=7523), [Steed's Toppling Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7993)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Faithful Stride](/Feats.aspx?ID=7992) <actions string="Two Actions or Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 71

**Prerequisites**
[Faithful Steed](/Feats.aspx?ID=5885)

**Requirements**
You are riding your mount.

</column>

---

Confident in your faith, you [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) to order your mount to Stride up to twice its Speed (or up to three times its Speed if you used 3 actions for Faithful Stride). During this movement, your mount can Stride across liquid and other surfaces that don't support its weight. If your mount ends its movement on a surface that can't support it, your mount (and you) fall in or it collapses as normal.

[Fake It Till You Make it](/Feats.aspx?ID=3809) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 127

**Archetype** [Alter Ego](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=187)

**Prerequisites**
[Alter Ego Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3807)

</column>

---

When you take on a role, you become more capable with all sorts of tasks involving that role. When you Assume a Role, choose two skills associated with the role in some way; if you're untrained, you can use your level as your proficiency bonus for those skills, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to skill checks with those skills as long as you remain in that role. You and the GM determine which skills you assume.

    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fake Out](/Feats.aspx?ID=3161) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=163" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 112

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) For the purpose of gunslinger feats and abilities, if the ability states that you fire your weapon, you fire your weapon; if it does not state as such, you do not have to fire your weapon. Notably, Fake Out does not require you to actually fire your weapon._

**Trigger**
An ally is about to use an action that requires an attack roll, targeting a creature within your weapon's first range increment.

**Requirements**
You're wielding a loaded firearm or crossbow.

</column>

---

With a skilled flourish of your weapon, you force an enemy to acknowledge you as a threat. Make an attack roll to [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) the triggering attack. If you dealt damage to that enemy with the same weapon since the start of your last turn, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to this roll.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs=""
>
[False Faith](/Feats.aspx?ID=1144) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=26" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City](/Sources.aspx?ID=13) pg. 63

**Prerequisites**
worshipper of [Droskar](/Deities.aspx?ID=28)

</column>

---

Droskar knows you may need to disguise yourself in societies that oppose your faith. After spending 1 hour in prayer to Droskar, you can cast spells using the religious symbol of a different deity as your divine focus, and you can address verbal prayers to that deity. Droskar intercepts your prayers and answers them without the named god knowing.

 This ability applies to the religious symbol of only one god at a time—making a different religious symbol work in this fashion requires another hour of prayer and causes the old one to cease functioning. You can always use a religious symbol of Droskar without affecting this ability.

fields.text: Feat 1 False Faith Cleric Source Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City pg. 63 Prerequisites worshipper of Droskar Droskar knows you may need to disguise yourself in societies that oppose your faith. After spending 1 hour in prayer to Droskar, you can cast spells using the religious symbol of a different deity as your divine focus, and you can address verbal prayers to that deity. Droskar intercepts your prayers and answers them without the named god knowing. This ability applies to the religious symbol of only one god at a time—making a different religious symbol work in this fashion requires another hour of prayer and causes the old one to cease functioning. You can always use a religious symbol of Droskar without affecting this ability.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[False Priest Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6935) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tanuki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=830" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 67

**Prerequisites**
[Everyday Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6930)

</column>

---

Nobody respects tanuki, but most everyone respects an esteemed priest, so what better form to take if you want to get by a little easier? When you Change Shape, you can assume the shape of a priest or other religious official from a religion of your choosing. While in your false priest form, you can attempt [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about Religion, and you can cast [_divine lance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1498) and [_haunting hymn_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1999) as [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4) [innate](/Rules.aspx?ID=2901) cantrips. If you critically fail at a Deception check while in your false priest form, your transformation is broken, returning you to your tanuki form, and you’re so embarrassed that you can’t resume your False Priest Form until your next daily preparations, after you’ve taken a night to sleep on it.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Familiar Master Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1970) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 174

**Archetype** [Familiar Master](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=60)

</column>

---

You have forged a mystical bond with a creature. This might have involved complex rituals and invocations, such as meditating under the moon until something crept out of the forest. Or maybe you just did each other a good turn, such as rescuing the beast from a trap or a foe, and then being rescued in turn. Whatever the details, you are now comrades until the end. You gain a [familiar](/Familiars.aspx). If you already have a familiar, you gain the [Enhanced Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=318) feat.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the familiar master archetype.

<title level="2">Familiar Master Dedication leads to...</title>
[Familiar Conduit](/Feats.aspx?ID=1972), [Familiar Mascot](/Feats.aspx?ID=1971), [Improved Familiar (Familiar Master)](/Feats.aspx?ID=1973), [Mutable Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=1974), [Scion of Domora Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=4106)

Or maybe you just did each other a good turn, such as rescuing the beast from a trap or a foe, and then being rescued in turn. Whatever the details, you are now comrades until the end. You gain a familiar. If you already have a familiar, you gain the Enhanced Familiar feat. Special You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the familiar master archetype. Familiar Master Dedication leads to... [Familiar Master Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6328) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 200

**Archetype** [Familiar Master](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=250)

---

You have forged a mystical bond with a creature. This might have involved complex rituals and invocations, such as meditating under the moon until something crept out of the forest. Or maybe you just did each other a good turn, such as rescuing the beast from a trap or a foe, and then being rescued in turn. Whatever the details, you are now comrades until the end. You gain a [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=160). If you already have a familiar, you gain the [Enhanced Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=4717) feat.

<title level="2">Familiar Master Dedication leads to...</title>
[Familiar Conduit](/Feats.aspx?ID=6330), [Familiar Mascot](/Feats.aspx?ID=6329), [Improved Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=6331), [Mutable Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=6332), [Scion of Domora Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8124)

</title>

<traits>

Your familiar’s magical presence can serve as an aspect of a ritual. When you cast a ritual, your familiar can serve as a secondary caster, fulfilling any requirements for the secondary caster as well as a secondary check. You can’t replace a secondary caster who’s the target of the spell.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 116

**Prerequisites**
You have a [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=2121), and you're able to [cast spells](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734).

</column>

---

You’ve forged an empowered mystical bond with your familiar. You gain the [Enhanced Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=4717) feat, increasing your familiar’s number of abilities.

**Special** You can take Familiar Sage Dedication even if you haven’t yet gained three feats from the [familiar master](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=250) archetype, and you can take Familiar Master Dedication even if you haven’t yet gained three feats from the familiar sage archetype. You can’t select another dedication feat until you’ve gained two other feats from the familiar master or familiar sage archetypes.

<title level="2">Familiar Sage Dedication leads to...</title>
[Familiar Ritualist](/Feats.aspx?ID=7099), [Familiar's Resolve](/Feats.aspx?ID=7096), [Fulu Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=7097), [Golden Dragon's Bounty](/Feats.aspx?ID=7100), [Lightning Rings' Intervention](/Feats.aspx?ID=7101), [Lightning Rings' Overcharge](/Feats.aspx?ID=7103), [Phoenix's Flight](/Feats.aspx?ID=7105), [Seal of the Golden Dragon](/Feats.aspx?ID=7102), [Tempest Cloud's Speed](/Feats.aspx?ID=7098), [Vexing Tempest](/Feats.aspx?ID=7104)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Familiar's Eyes](/Feats.aspx?ID=1582) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=323" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 104

**Prerequisites**
a familiar

</column>

---

You use your familiar's senses as easily as your own. You project your senses into your familiar. When you do, you lose all sensory information from your own body, but you can sense through your familiar's body until you Dismiss the effect. While projecting your senses in this way, you can converse telepathically with your familiar if it understands a language.

**Special** This feat has the trait corresponding to the tradition of spells you cast ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Familiar's Language](/Feats.aspx?ID=1569) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=323" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 102

**Prerequisites**
a familiar

</column>

---

You've learned to speak with your familiar and other creatures like it. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) skill with creatures of the same family of animals as your familiar. For example, if your familiar were a cat, you could gain the effects of speak with animals for any felines (including leopards, lions, and tigers, among others). This ability doesn't make them more friendly than normal. If your familiar ever changes to a different creature, you can't use this ability for 1 week while you absorb your new familiar's language.

**Special** This feat has the trait corresponding to the tradition of spells you cast ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)).

[Fan Dancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7039) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 98

**Archetype** [Fan Dancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=276)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45)

**Access**
Tian Xia origin

</column>

---

You sweep across the battlefield, manifesting both the gentle spring breeze and the crisp autumn gusts. You become an expert in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45). At 7th level you become a master in Performance, and at 15th level, you become legendary in Performance. Whenever you [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390) while holding a fan, you can give your Feint the [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=527) trait. If you do, you can Stride 10 feet before or after as part of the same action.

<title level="2">Fan Dancer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Close Formation](/Feats.aspx?ID=7047), [Dizzying Spin Dance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7048), [Dragon's Journey](/Feats.aspx?ID=7052), [Fluttering Distraction](/Feats.aspx?ID=7049), [Fluttering Misdirection](/Feats.aspx?ID=7043), [Peony's Flourish](/Feats.aspx?ID=7051), [Petal Step](/Feats.aspx?ID=7040), [Pushing Wind](/Feats.aspx?ID=7045), [Solo Dancer](/Feats.aspx?ID=7041), [Sweeping Fan Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=7044), [Sweeping Fan Redirection](/Feats.aspx?ID=7050), [Twirl Through](/Feats.aspx?ID=7042), [Twirling Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7046)

Whenever you Feint while holding a fan, you can give your Feint the air trait. If you do, you can Stride 10 feet before or after as part of the same action. Fan Dancer Dedication leads to... Close Formation, Dizzying Spin Dance, Dragon's Journey, Fluttering Distraction, Fluttering Misdirection, Peony's Flourish, Petal Step, Pushing Wind, Solo Dancer, Sweeping Fan Block, Sweeping Fan Redirection, Twirl Through, Twirling Strike

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fane's Escape](/Feats.aspx?ID=2267) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 118

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All characters have access to this feat._

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

**Access**
Member of the Pathfinder Society.

**Requirements**
You have a deck of [playing cards](/Equipment.aspx?ID=873) in your possession.

</column>

---

A good getaway requires a good distraction. You Interact to draw a deck of cards and flip it in a fluttering explosion, causing you to become briefly [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) to all other creatures using vision as their precise sense, and then you [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63). You have enough cover to Sneak until the end of your turn. This leaves all of the cards from the deck scattered about the room; collecting them into a deck again takes several minutes.

<title level="2">Perilous Larceny</title>

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 118

Pirate captain Stella Fane (CN female human privateer; _Lost Omens Character Guide_ 119) joined the Pathfinder Society as a venture-captain as part of a deal to help the Society make it through the heavily armed naval blockades of Port Peril's Free Captains. Cunning and competitive, Stella's greatest weakness as a leader of the Society is her uncompromising hatred of the Chelaxian government. Those who can avoid ending up sunk or executed by Chelaxian naval commanders while assisting Stella may leave with a few more tricks than they had before seeing the skilled pirate in action. Fane's Fourberie and Stella's Stab and Snag, below, are class feats that rogues or swashbucklers can select. When you select either feat, it loses the trait from the other class.

**Related Feats**: [Fane's Fourberie](/Feats.aspx?ID=2266), [Stella's Stab and Snag](/Feats.aspx?ID=2268)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fane's Fourberie](/Feats.aspx?ID=2266) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=139" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=152" />
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=321" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 118

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All characters have access to this feat. A character with the Fane’s Fourberie feat can etch their deck of cards with weapon runes themself or have this service provided by a third party. The deck can also be targeted by weapon-modifying effects such as a magic weapon spell._

**Access**
Member of the Pathfinder Society.

</column>

---

Stella Fane has perfected a technique for using playing cards as weapons that's one part sleight of hand and one part magic. When you enter this stance, choose whether to treat [playing cards](/Equipment.aspx?ID=873) in your possession as [daggers](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3) or [darts](/Weapons.aspx?ID=68); you can wield a playing card in all ways as the chosen weapon until the stance ends. As long as the majority of the deck remains in your possession, any cards that are lost or thrown can be found after 1 minute. Otherwise, the remaining cards are likely lost or destroyed.

 A character who has this feat can enchant a single deck of playing cards as a magic weapon, etching fundamental and property runes directly onto the deck of cards.

<title level="2">Perilous Larceny</title>

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 118

Pirate captain Stella Fane (CN female human privateer; _Lost Omens Character Guide_ 119) joined the Pathfinder Society as a venture-captain as part of a deal to help the Society make it through the heavily armed naval blockades of Port Peril's Free Captains. Cunning and competitive, Stella's greatest weakness as a leader of the Society is her uncompromising hatred of the Chelaxian government. Those who can avoid ending up sunk or executed by Chelaxian naval commanders while assisting Stella may leave with a few more tricks than they had before seeing the skilled pirate in action.     right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fang Sharpener](/Feats.aspx?ID=1000) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Goblin" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=81" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 37

**Prerequisites**
[Irongut Goblin](/Heritages.aspx?ID=17) heritage or [Razortooth Goblin](/Heritages.aspx?ID=18) heritage

</column>

---

You have filed your teeth into jagged points and have an unusually powerful jaw, making your mouth a dangerous weapon. If you’re an irongut goblin, you gain a jaws unarmed attack that deals 1d4 piercing damage, and if you’re a razortooth goblin, your jaws unarmed attack deals 1d8 piercing damage and loses the finesse trait. Whenever you score a critical hit with your jaws unarmed attack, your target takes 1 [persistent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) bleed damage per weapon damage die.

<title level="2">Fang Sharpener leads to...</title>
[Ankle Bite](/Feats.aspx?ID=1002), [Hungry Goblin](/Feats.aspx?ID=1008)

<traits>
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

---

You launch yourself through the air at a foe. Attempt a High Jump or Long Jump. If you attempt a High Jump, determine the height of your jump as though determining the length of a Long Jump. At the end of your jump, you can make a melee Strike. 

After your Strike, you fall to the ground if you’re in the air. If the distance of your fall is no more than the height of your jump, you take no damage and land upright.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Farabellus Flip](/Feats.aspx?ID=2275) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Barbarian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=18" />
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=136" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 119

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All characters have access to this feat._

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1); trained in medium armor

**Access**
Member of the Pathfinder Society.

**Trigger**
An enemy targets you with a melee Strike.

</column>

---

Surprisingly agile even in a breastplate and carrying a full rucksack, Marcos Farabellus developed this evasive maneuver during one of his many adventures. Flinging your body into a twisting somersault, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your AC against the triggering attack. If the attack still hits you, you can Step to an open space that's still within the triggering enemy's reach, turning the impact of the blow into momentum.

<title level="2">Swords Training</title>

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 119

Marcos Farabellus (_Lost Omens Pathfinder Society Guide_ page 50) is a talented swordsman and likely the most beloved of the Society's three deans. In addition to teaching his students about the dangers of exploring ruins through energetic and performative lectures, Farabellus also teaches his favorite students a few of the martial techniques he's developed over his illustrious career. The Farabellus Flip is a class feat for barbarians, fighters, or rangers. When you select the feat, it loses the traits from the other classes.

**Related Feats**: [Discerning Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=2274)

    right="Feat 1"

[Fascinated by Society](/Feats.aspx?ID=5299) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Awakened Animal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=787" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 25

</column>

---

Just as some humanoids find themselves driven to study nature, you are obsessed with the artificial constructs of society and can't get enough. You are trained in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47). If you would automatically become trained in Society, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

 As a newcomer, sometimes your understanding is a bit off target. When you fail, but don't critically fail, a Society check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) or [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363), you learn the correct information (as you would on a success) and erroneous information (as you would on a critical failure). You don't have any way to differentiate which is which.

>
[Fascinating Performance](/Feats.aspx?ID=5147) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 255

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12)

</column>

---

When you Perform, compare your result to the Will DC of one observer. If you succeed, the target is [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) by you for 1 round. If the observer is in a situation that demands immediate attention, such as combat, you must critically succeed to fascinate it and the [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=2401) action gains the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) trait. You must choose which creature you're trying to fascinate before you roll your check, and the target is then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

If you're an expert in Performance, you can fascinate up to four observers; if you're a master, you can fascinate up to 10 observers; and if you're legendary, you can fascinate any number of observers at the same time.

<title level="2">Fascinating Performance leads to...</title>
[Focused Fascination](/Feats.aspx?ID=6131)

Your body quickly bounces back from afflictions. You regain twice as many Hit Points from resting. In addition, you reduce the severity of your drained condition by 2 when you rest for a night instead of by 1.

>
[Fated Duel](/Feats.aspx?ID=7414) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 137

**Archetype** [Prophesied Monarch](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=294)

**Frequency**
once per week

**Prerequisites**
[Prophesied Monarch Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7403)

</column>

---

You and your knights are an unbeatable force together, but sometimes it’s a monarch’s duty to resolve the fate of their kingdom with nothing more than their own trusted weapon. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320), and choose one opponent within 30 feet; you declare a Fated Duel against that opponent. 

If the opponent accepts your challenge, you’re locked in mystical combat together. Neither you nor your opponent can move more than 30 feet from each other; you both can’t be harmed by any creature other than each other; and you both can’t harm any creature other than each other. This mystical bond is incredibly draining on both parties, pulling at their life and spirit; if neither you nor your opponent has defeated the other by the time 1 minute has passed, you both become [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) 1. Your doomed conditions increase by 1 for each additional minute that passes until one or both of you die.

If your opponent refuses your challenge, you regain a Mythic Point and can immediately attempt an [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) check at mythic proficiency to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) them.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Tiefling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=258" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 32

</column>

---

You bear a grudge, inherited from a blasphemous [asura](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=218) forebear in your bloodline, against a particular deity and their works. You also have some vestigial signs of your previous incarnation, such as a second set of shoulder blades without usable arms, a set of mostly closed eyes where no eyes belong, or strange scarring reminiscent of a mouth.

 You gain the Find Fault reaction.

 **Find Fault** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Trigger** You attempt a saving throw against a spell or magic effect but haven't rolled yet; **Effect** You find some kind of fault with the magic, using that flaw to protect yourself from the effect. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your saving throw against the triggering effect, which increases to a +2 circumstance bonus if the effect is [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) and originates from a worshipper of the deity you chose for your grudge.

<title level="2">Faultspawn leads to...</title>
[Asura Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=3940), [Dominion Aura](/Feats.aspx?ID=3943), [Towering Presence](/Feats.aspx?ID=3939)

The benefit doesn’t apply against favored enemies disguised as other creatures, and the GM determines whether it applies against a creature disguised as a favored enemy.

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 158 **Archetypes** [Steel Falcon](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=374) (Level 6), [Nidalese Horselord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=381) (Level 4) --- You have studied a specific terrain to overcome its challenges. Choose aquatic, arctic, desert, forest, mountain, plains, sky, swamp, or underground as your favored terrain. When in that terrain, you can ignore the effects of non-magical difficult terrain. If you have the unimpeded journey class feature, you gain a second benefit while in your favored terrain, depending on your choice:
  • **Aquatic** You gain a swim Speed equal to your Speed. If you already had a swim Speed, you instead gain a +10-foot status bonus to your swim Speed.
  • **Arctic** You need to eat and drink only one-tenth as much as usual, you aren’t affected by severe or extreme cold, and you can walk across ice and snow at full Speed without needing to Balance.
  • **Desert** You need to eat and drink only one-tenth as much as usual, you aren’t affected by severe or extreme heat, and you can walk along sand at full Speed without needing to Balance.
  • **Forest, Mountain, or Underground** You gain a climb Speed equal to your Speed. If you already had a climb Speed, you instead gain a +10-foot status bonus to your climb Speed.
  • **Plains** You gain a +10-foot status bonus to your land Speed.
  • **Sky** You gain a +10-foot status bonus to your fly Speed, if you have one.
  • **Swamp** You can move across bogs at full Speed, even if they are deep enough to be greater difficult terrain or to normally require you to Swim.
Favored Terrain leads to... [Terrain Master](/Feats.aspx?ID=4885)

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=590" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 77

**Archetype** [Werecreature](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=225)

**Prerequisites**
[Werecreature Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5486); weretiger

**Requirements**
You’re in hybrid or tiger shape and your last action was a critically successful Strike with your unarmed attack.

</column>

---

You attack with a feline grace as captivatingly beautiful as it is deadly. All enemies within 30 feet of the creature you critically hit must attempt at a Will save against your class DC. Enemies that fail their saves become [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) and are [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) with you for 1 round. Your [hostile actions](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) don't end this fascination, but those of your allies do. Regardless of the effects of the save, the creature is immune to Fearful Symmetry for 1 hour.

<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 22

a familiar

</column>

---

Your familiar trades places with an elemental from its elemental plane. Summon a common creature that has the [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) trait and a level no greater than your level – 4. This creature gains the [summoned](/Traits.aspx?ID=706) trait. This creature appears in the same space as your familiar, which disappears for the duration of this impulse. You can Sustain this impulse up to 1 minute. When the impulse ends, the familiar appears in the space the summoned elemental occupied. A familiar can endure this process only so often—if you use this impulse on your familiar more than once per day, it dies as soon as it returns the second time.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 60

**Archetype** [Zombie](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=182)

[Zombie Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3557)

**Requirements**
You are adjacent to a [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) or [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) creature, or a deceased creature that died in the past hour.

</column>

---

You feast upon an adjacent restrained or unconscious creature, or a deceased creature that died in the past hour. If the creature is alive, you deal damage equal to your jaws damage. Whether it's alive or not, you gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to half your level that last for 1 minute.

 You can instead choose to gain temporary Hit Points equal to double your level, but if you do, you must succeed at a DC 6 flat check or your body deteriorates.

---

You learn the [fortifying brew](/Rituals.aspx?ID=147) ritual, but you instead prepare dishes for a lavish meal that have the same effect as the drinks from the normal version of the ritual. You perform both aspects of the ritual yourself, acting as both primary and a secondary caster. You must still attempt the secondary check normally performed by a secondary caster. In addition, you can use [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) or Cooking [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) for both the primary and secondary checks. The ritual gains the [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) trait as nature spirits attend to you and your guests.

</traits>

---

To blend in with the grounded and wingless, you fold your wings just so on your back, creating the illusion of a feathered cloak. You receive a +2 circumstance bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) a version of yourself who is not a strix.

 Additionally, your folded wings help you obscure objects on your person, providing a +2 circumstance bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks to [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=61).

If you've taken a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against it this round, your result can be no better than a failure. **Critical Success** You and the target are considered allies until the end of your next turn or until you take a hostile action against it, whichever comes first. **Failure** No effect.
**Critical Failure** The target knows you attempted to fool it and plays along. You're [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to the target until the beginning of your next turn.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 79

</column>

---

Your [bestial mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=82) brings out the beast lurking within you, granting you especially sharp claws and teeth as well as a ferocious appearance. Whenever you’re affected by a bestial mutagen, you gain the mutagen’s item bonus to your Intimidation checks. In addition, your claws and jaws are increasingly vicious, and they gain the [deadly d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174) trait. Finally, you can increase the mutagen’s penalty to AC from –1 to –2 and, in exchange, increase the damage die size of your claws and jaws by one step.

---

Since ancient times, the mightiest orc beast tamers would draw out the true fighting spirit of their companion beasts by feeding the creatures a draft incorporating the orc's own blood. Animal companions or bonded animals you have gain the Orc Ferocity feat, and they gain a reaction they can use only for Orc Ferocity. If you have the Undying Ferocity ancestry feat, all animal companions or bonded animals you have also gain the benefits of that feat when using the Orc Ferocity reaction.

 **Ferocious Charge** <actions string="Two Actions" /> The companion Strides up to twice its Speed in a straight line and makes an antlers, head, or horn Strike. <traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Lizardfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=760" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 45

**Prerequisites**
[River Adaptation](/Feats.aspx?ID=6864)

**Requirements**
You are [swimming](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) and have a free hand.

</column>

---

The waters around you permit you passage, a privilege you can share with a willing ally. You hold on to an adjacent ally and [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381), carrying them along with you. If you spend three actions Ferrying through Waves, you instead Swim twice. If your ally would need to attempt any [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to Swim while you’re Ferrying through Waves, you roll the check and your result applies to them.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Disease" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=46" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 61

**Archetype** [Zombie](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=182)

**Prerequisites**
[Zombie Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3557)

</column>

---

Wounds you inflict with your [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks fester and rot, becoming infected and difficult to heal. The DC to [Treat these Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=57) using [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) increases by 5, and magically or alchemically healing these wounds requires a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Succeeding at any of these removes the disease. The effect also ends if the creature is healed to full Hit Points by any means.

    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Feverish Enzymes](/Feats.aspx?ID=3507) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 49

**Archetype** [Ghoul](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=178)

**Prerequisites**
[Ghoul Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3504)

</column>

---

Your claws and fangs exude an infectious enzyme, related to the necrotic effects of ghoul fever, that causes a creature's wounds to heal slowly. Strike with your claw or jaws. This attack deals negative damage instead of its normal type; on a hit, the target halves any healing it receives until the start of your next turn. The target or an adjacent ally can spend two Interact actions to squeeze the enzymes from the wound and remove the effect.

 If you are satiated, when you hit you can choose to end your satiation and boost your enzymes, increasing the duration to 1 minute.

<title level="2">Feverish Enzymes leads to...</title>
[Paralyzing Slash](/Feats.aspx?ID=3509)

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 127 **Prerequisites** [Fey Influence](/Feats.aspx?ID=1239) --- The fey influence on your form and features grows even more powerful and notable. You gain one of the following features and abilities; this must be the same animal or fey type as you chose for Fey Influence.
  • **Anteater** You become an expert in primal DCs and spell attack rolls. You can cast [_slow_](/Spells.aspx?ID=289) as an innate primal spell once per day.
  • **Cat Sith** You laugh off the outraged curses of those you have tricked or wronged. Whenever a creature targets you with a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=110) effect, make a DC 13 flat check. On a success, you are unaffected.
  • **Cursed Bluebird** You have enough control over your curse to turn a bane into a minor blessing. Once per day, you can temporarily transform yourself or an ally into a blue bird, as a 4th-level [_pest form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=217) (bird only) targeting one willing creature.
  • **Dryad** Your hair becomes intermixed with delicate but razor-edged leaves that move as you command. You gain a leaves ranged unarmed attack that deals 1d6 slashing damage. Your leaves are in the [dart](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=6) weapon group and have the [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103) and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) traits.
  • **Faun** You can cast [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=34), [_sleep_](/Spells.aspx?ID=288), and [_triple time_](/Spells.aspx?ID=392) as innate primal spells once per day each. Whenever you cast one of these spells, you can Step or Stride as part of the activity.
  • **Gremlin** You become an expert in primal DCs and spell attack rolls. You can cast [_mad monkeys_](/Spells.aspx?ID=702) as an innate primal spell once per day.
  • **Monarch** Once per day, you gain the ability to manifest a pair of exquisite butterfly wings. These wings remain for 10 minutes. You gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed while you've manifested your wings.
  • **Unicorn** You become trained in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9), or an expert if you were already trained. You gain a +2 status bonus to saves against [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) and [charm](/Traits.aspx?ID=247) effects.
**Special** This feat gains the trait appropriate for your ancestry ([human](/Traits.aspx?ID=90) for [human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=6), [goblin](/Traits.aspx?ID=81) for [goblin](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=4), etc.).

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

Your enhanced fey connection affords you a warmer reception from creatures of the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=10) as well as tools to foil their tricks. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to both Perception checks and saving throws against [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69).

 In addition, whenever you meet a fey creature in a social situation, you can immediately attempt a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) check to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) on that creature rather than needing to converse for 1 minute. You take a –5 penalty to the check. If you fail, you can engage in 1 minute of conversation and attempt a new check at the end of that time rather than accepting the failure or critical failure result.

**Special** If you have the [Glad-Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=787) skill feat, you don’t take the penalty on your immediate Diplomacy check if the target is a fey.

This does not grant access to any additional feats._ --- You have been exposed to powerful fey magic. You become trained in primal DCs and spell attack rolls. You gain the [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69) trait and one of the following features that grants an innate primal spell that can be used once per day.
  • **Anteater** You can launch your tongue forward as a deadly attack, gaining [_grim tendrils_](/Spells.aspx?ID=141).
  • **[Cat Sith](/Monsters.aspx?ID=517)** You have catlike features and can appear as a mundane cat with [_pest form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=217) (cat only).
  • **Cursed Bluebird** You have blue feathers or wings. It's terrible luck to harm a bluebird, and you can manifest that power as [_ill omen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=696).
  • **[Dryad](/Monsters.aspx?ID=312)** Your body is covered in elegant vines, granting you [_summon plant or fungus_](/Spells.aspx?ID=325).
  • **Faun** Your legs and feet are swift and possibly hooved, granting you [_fleet step_](/Spells.aspx?ID=122).
  • **[Gremlin](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=58)** You have long, bat-like ears and gain [_bane_](/Spells.aspx?ID=18).
  • **Monarch** You have vestigial, insectile features and gain [_spider sting_](/Spells.aspx?ID=300).
  • **[Unicorn](/Monsters.aspx?ID=397)** You have a magical horn or a prominent symbol of one on your forehead, which you can use to cast [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148).
**Special** This feat gains the trait appropriate for your ancestry ([human](/Traits.aspx?ID=90) for [human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=6), [goblin](/Traits.aspx?ID=81) for [goblin](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=4), etc.). Fey Influence leads to... [Cannibalize Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=4049), [Drain Emotion](/Feats.aspx?ID=4047), [Eldritch Calm](/Feats.aspx?ID=4051), [Fey Ascension](/Feats.aspx?ID=4048), [Fey Transcendence](/Feats.aspx?ID=4052), [Glamour](/Feats.aspx?ID=4050)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Fey Life](/Feats.aspx?ID=3759) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 57

**Prerequisites**
You helped to save a [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69) from a terrible fate, and you're not a fey.

</column>

---

There are some fates worse than death–and you worked to save a fey from one such fate. In return, your life became bound to theirs. Fey magic has since become a part of you, bringing the vibrant colors of the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=10) to you and all that surrounds you. Your skin, hair, all that you touch, and anything within 5 feet of you changes to the most brilliant hues possible, though the colors fade as you cease to touch an object or you move away. You gain the ability to cast [_summon fey_](/Spells.aspx?ID=322) as a 7th-level primal innate spell once per day. At 18th level the spell heightens to 8th level, and at 20th level it heightens to 9th level.

 The first time you die after gaining this feat, the bond you made with the fey invokes the power of the First World to return you to life. Immediately after dying, you revive, becoming conscious (and [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=42) as normal) at 27 Hit Points, and you gain the fey trait. Your eyes become a rainbow of colors, and you take on a visual aspect of the fey with whom you are bound, such as by growing wings, horns, or a plantlike body. The change has no mechanical effect; for instance, the wings wouldn't allow you to fly, nor would horns grant a horn unarmed attack.

 The second time you die, you reawaken in the First World with the full appearance of the fey that was bound to you. You become an NPC, unconcerned with your old mortal life. You can be returned to your previous life in the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) by having allies spend 3 days building a shrine to the First World, giving three offerings that hold deep sentimental value for you or another, and holding a raucous, three-day long feast.

 Any time that you die after that, you reawaken again in the First World with no memories of your previous life, and you can only be brought back by powerful magic such as a [_wish_](/Spells.aspx?ID=377) spell.

You become a powerful fey creature, gaining strengths tied to the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=10) but also some of the weakness against which all fey must contend. You gain a +2 status bonus to saves against [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), and [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61) effects, and you can use [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) on and to make very simple [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) of [animals](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) and [plants](/Traits.aspx?ID=125). **Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 58 **Archetype** [Field Propagandist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=326) **Prerequisites** Charisma +2; Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38); Trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) --- Having devoted your life to crafting propaganda, you know that winning the hearts and minds of soldiers can be a deciding factor in securing the successful outcome of a war. You gain the Spread Propaganda exploration activity (see below). While you are not immune to propaganda, you are resistant to it. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Perception DC against attempts made by others to Lie to you. If you have the [Lie to Me](/Feats.aspx?ID=5177) skill feat, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception DC. You become trained in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47). If you were already trained, you become an expert instead. **Spread Propaganda** (exploration, secret) You spread propaganda about a faction (which may include an army, organization, or other particular group of people). This takes as long as it would normally take for you to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391) (typically 2 hours). At the end of this time, the GM rolls a secret Deception check to see how effective you were at spreading propaganda.
**Critical Success** Your propaganda spreads effectively, and for the next month, creatures that succeed on checks to Gather Information learn your propaganda over facts about the subject. It cannot be traced back to you. You also learn information as if you succeeded at a [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) check about the faction.
**Success** As critical success, but the propaganda persists for 1 week and can be traced back to you by a character who critically succeeds at the skill check to Gather Information.
**Failure** Your propaganda fails to take hold.
**Critical Failure** Your propaganda is stunningly ineffective, and you take a –4 circumstance penalty to Deception checks to spread propaganda about the same subject for 1 week. In addition, the subject and its enemies become aware that you attempted to spread propaganda. Field Propagandist Dedication leads to... [A Tale to Believe In](/Feats.aspx?ID=7928), [Fabricate Truth](/Feats.aspx?ID=7923), [Invented Vulnerability](/Feats.aspx?ID=7925), [Invincible Army](/Feats.aspx?ID=7926), [Mass Delusion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7930), [Orator's Fillibuster](/Feats.aspx?ID=7927), [Predispose Settlement](/Feats.aspx?ID=7924), [The Truth as I See it](/Feats.aspx?ID=7929)

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs=""
>
[Fiend Eternal](/Feats.aspx?ID=7330) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 113

**Archetype** [Archfiend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=288)

**Prerequisites**
[Archfiend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7320)

</column>

---

Through all your machinations and accumulation of power, you have completed your apotheosis and become a true archfiend. You gain the [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600) and [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) traits and are immune to your realm’s damage type. You don’t age. Your planned realm becomes a complete reality, forming within a section of [Hell](/Planes.aspx?ID=42), the [Outer Rifts](/Planes.aspx?ID=45), [the Netherworld](/Planes.aspx?ID=36), its own fiendish demiplane, or some other planar space of your choosing. If you have the [Seat of Power](/Feats.aspx?ID=7328) feat, that seat of power is grafted onto your realm and the [Enter Seat of Power](/Actions.aspx?ID=2988) activity transports you to any place within your realm; otherwise, you can enter and exit your realm in a similar fashion with a brief ritual that takes 10 minutes (though you can’t bring anyone with you).

Whenever you would die, you are instead reduced to 0 Hit Points, become [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), and are immediately transported to your seat of power within your realm. After 1 hour (or 1 round if you have the Seat of Power feat), you regain 5 Hit Points and reawaken. You can’t leave your realm until you’re fully healed or 1 week passes (whichever comes first).

In addition, you gain a small group of fiendish followers who reside in your realm. They never leave your realm (though one might occasionally come to your aid if you have the [Marshal Fiendish Forces](/Feats.aspx?ID=7324) feat), but they constantly spy on the mortal world to keep you informed. You are telepathically linked to these followers and can choose to speak with the group, or a specific fiend, as a three-action activity that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait. In doing so, you can avail yourself of the fiends’ surveillance to learn about the world or current events. You can either [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) on any topic or [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391). If you critically fail to do either, you get a failure instead.

You were raised by a tiefling or a fiendish relative, or you've devoted yourself to researching the secrets of the fiendish realms. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) and [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13). If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You possess fiendish magic. Choose two of the following spells: [_disguise magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1491), [_false vitality_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1523), [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1577), [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663), [_shatter_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1670), or [_paranoia_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1623). </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
<trait label="Oath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=119" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 110

**Prerequisites**
[tenets of good](/Tenets.aspx?ID=1)

</column>

---

You’ve sworn an oath to banish the corruption of fiends to the dark planes they call home. You gain the following edict: “You must banish or slay fiends you come across as long as you have a reasonable chance of success; in the incredibly unlikely event you find a fiend that isn't unholy, you don’t have to banish or kill it.”

 Your Retributive Strike gains a +4 circumstance bonus to damage against a fiend, or a +6 circumstance bonus if you have master proficiency with the weapon you used. Your Glimpse of Redemption’s resistance against damage from a fiend is 7 + your level. If you use Liberating Step triggered by a fiend, your ally gains a +4 circumstance bonus to checks granted by your Liberating Step, and the ally can Step twice afterward.

 You don’t consider fiends to be legitimate authorities, even in nations ruled by fiends.

<title level="2">Fiendsbane Oath leads to...</title>
[Anchoring Aura](/Feats.aspx?ID=249), [Banishing Blow](/Feats.aspx?ID=1242)

</title>

You challenge a single ally to a physical competition. This competition must involve accomplishing a specific goal for a specific use of the [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) or [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) skill, such as [Climbing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) to the top of a wall, [Tripping](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) a specific foe, or [Long Jumping](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378) across a chasm. You and your selected ally gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the associated skill check for 1 minute or until one of you wins the challenge, whichever is first. If you win this competition, you gain a +2 status bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks for 1 hour.

When you escape death, you return to life with retributive fire that burns those who harmed you. You expend 1 Mythic Point, return to consciousness, [Stand](/Actions.aspx?ID=2303), and regain additional Hit Points equal to your level. You then erupt in flames, dealing fire damage equal to twice your level to adjacent foes, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. Foes that critically fail the save are also [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 5 feet away from you.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 129

**Prerequisites**
[Eternal Legend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7374)

</column>

---

Mortal wounds that would kill other warriors are no more than the flutter of butterfly wings to you. When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points, you aren’t knocked [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) and you don’t gain the dying condition. Until the start of your next turn, you become [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to all damage, but you also can’t regain Hit Points in any way except the following. If you Strike and damage a foe on this turn, you regain 4d8+30 Hit Points. Otherwise, your [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99) value increases by 1 and you remain immune to damage and [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623). This cycle continues until you regain Hit Points by damaging a foe or until you reach wounded 4, at which point you lose the wounded condition, fall unconscious, and gain the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition.

fields.text: Feat 20 Fight Through Oblivion Mythic Source War of Immortals pg. 129 Archetype Eternal Legend Prerequisites Eternal Legend Dedication Mortal wounds that would kill other warriors are no more than the flutter of butterfly wings to you. When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points, you aren’t knocked unconscious and you don’t gain the dying condition. Until the start of your next turn, you become immune to all damage, but you also can’t regain Hit Points in any way except the following. If you Strike and damage a foe on this turn, you regain 4d8+30 Hit Points. Otherwise, your wounded value increases by 1 and you remain immune to damage and healing. This cycle continues until you regain Hit Points by damaging a foe or until you reach wounded 4, at which point you lose the wounded condition, fall unconscious, and gain the dying condition.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Final Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=2458) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Morph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=113" />
<trait label="Tiefling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=258" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 63

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

You embrace your monstrous blood and make it your own, screaming out to the heavens and hells alike in rage, pain, and defiance. Reality buckles and twists under your sudden power—each tiefling has a unique transformation, but it might include sulfurous flames, choruses of shrieks, or twisting, serpentine lightning. Every creature within 10 feet of you is [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) and [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for 1 round unless they succeed at a Fortitude save using your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Your final form has the effects of [_divine vessel_](/Spells.aspx?ID=85) for a deity that shares an alignment with your fiendish lineage. Your final form resembles a creature from your fiendish lineage, and you remain in that form for 1 minute. While in your final form, you can cast [_chilling darkness_](/Spells.aspx?ID=36), [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119), and [_lightning bolt_](/Spells.aspx?ID=172) as 6th-level divine innate spells, once each per use of this feat.

 When you emerge from your final form, you become [drained 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10). In addition, if you have this feat, you gain weakness 10 to good even when not in your final form, and you take good damage even if you aren't evil.

**Special** At the GM's discretion, the specific elements of this feat can be adjusted to better fit the tiefling's lineage—for example, a GM might decide that a particular [beastbrood](/Feats.aspx?ID=2449) tiefling could cast a 6th-level [_phantasmal killer_](/Spells.aspx?ID=219) instead of _fireball_.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

As stubborn in death as you are in life, you vow you'll never aid your hated enemies. You can't be transformed into an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), except by effects that originate from an [artifact](/Traits.aspx?ID=253) or deity. Undead creatures that touch your corpse take 1 positive damage each time they do, or 1d6 positive damage each time they expose themselves to your corpse in a more thorough manner, such as by biting or carrying your corpse.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Final Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=3208) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 119

**Requirements**
You're wielding an unloaded firearm.

</column>

---

You jam a triple charge of black powder into your weapon to unleash a devastating but risky and inaccurate attack. Interact to reload, expending three doses of black powder in addition to your normal black powder or ammunition, then Strike with your firearm against a creature within the weapon's first range increment. If you roll a success, the attack is instead a critical success, but if you roll a failure, the weapon [misfires](/Rules.aspx?ID=1649). Regardless of your roll, after the attack you're [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) until the start of your next turn and [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs=""
>
[Final Shot Knows the Way](/Feats.aspx?ID=8187) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
<trait label="Press" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=133" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 87

**Archetype** [Warshard Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=341)

**Prerequisites**
[Warshard Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8178)

**Requirements**
You are wielding a ranged warshard weapon and used it to make a ranged Strike against a foe this round.

</column>

---

You judge a foe’s defenses after attacking them and channel that knowledge into your warshard weapon and its ammunition. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323), then Stride twice. At any point during this movement, attempt a ranged Strike at mythic proficiency with your warshard weapon against the same foe you already attacked this round. This Strike ignores any modifiers from cover or concealment the target may have, as the ammunition weaves and twists through the air in an impossible flight. All penalties from range increments are negated during this Strike. If this shot hits its target, the target is so astounded by the shot that they become [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the end of your next turn.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Final Union](/Feats.aspx?ID=9162) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Necromancer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=950" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 41

**Prerequisites**
[Bind Heroic Spirit](/Feats.aspx?ID=9114)

</column>

---

You and the heroic spirit have formed an eternal pact and now share your body. You are constantly under the effect of a 10th-rank bind heroic spirit. You choose whether the heroic spirit remains as a separate entity bound to you or whether you become a fused spirit that lives in unison, possibly identifying as an entirely new person.

You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) feat for a topic the spirit knew in life, usually [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41).

If you would fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), you don’t fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) or drop any items. Instead, your heroic spirit takes control of your body, allowing you to perform actions as if you were still conscious. If you would die, your heroic spirit puppets your corpse for up to 1 minute after your death or until your body is destroyed. While dead, you are an undead object, granting you [immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=1609) to [bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), [death effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=2331), [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [nonlethal attacks](/Rules.aspx?ID=2311), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), and [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510), as well as the [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), and unconscious conditions. As an object, you have 200 Hit Points and a [Broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60) Threshold of 100 Hit Points. While broken, you are [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1. If you are destroyed, your body must be mended before you can be brought back to life. A creature can spend 8 hours to attempt a DC 45 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check, mending your body on a success. Alternatively, powerful magic such as the [_remake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1649) spell or the [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual can also be used to mend your body.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 54

**Archetype** [Trapsmith](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=111)

**Prerequisites**
[Trapsmith Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3134)

</column>

---

You've learned how to build [snares](/Equipment.aspx?Category=31) that trigger based on visual stimuli. When you construct a snare using gears, you can cause it to trigger based on the visual features of a creature. For example, you could lay a snare that can only be triggered by a Large or Larger creatures, or one that only activates when a creature wearing red clothing would trigger it. You can use this ability to specify your snares to trigger on creatures that typically do not trigger snares, such as creatures smaller than Small, though the creature must still otherwise satisfy the snare's trigger as normal.

[Finest Trick](/Feats.aspx?ID=2457) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tiefling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=258" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 63

**Prerequisites**
[Devil in Plain Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=2452)

</column>

---

Many fiends—[rakshasa rajas](/Monsters.aspx?ID=345) and [demonic succubi](/Monsters.aspx?ID=98) most famously—can take on the forms of others. With practice, you can do the same. When you use Devil in Plain Sight, you can alter your appearance to match a generic member of your base ancestry, rather than one that's obviously you without your tieflings features. In addition, you can imitate a specific person's appearance (of any ancestry of the same size and kind as your base ancestry, typically a [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=91) for most ancestries) if you consume a bit of their blood, a lock of their hair, or appropriate equivalents as part of the action. You still must know what the creature looks like, and you must be aware that the consumed portion comes from their body.

    right="Feat 20"

>
[Finish Their Story!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7390) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 129

**Archetype** [Eternal Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=292)

**Prerequisites**
[Eternal Legend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7374)

</column>

---

Though your tale is immortal, your foes aren’t afforded such an advantage and mainly serve only to further your legend. When the time is right, you can shepherd a weaker opponent off this mortal coil. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) and make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) at mythic proficiency against an enemy. This Strike counts as two attacks for your multiple attack penalty and either kills or damages the target depending on their level, as noted below. After you make this Strike, the target becomes temporarily immune to Finish Their Story!, for 1 hour.

**16th Level or Lower** If the Strike hits, the target dies instantly.

**17th Level** If the Strike hits, the target takes the Strike’s normal damage plus an additional three damage die.

**18th Level or Higher** If the Strike hits, the target takes the Strike’s normal damage plus an additional two damage die.

A lifetime of proximity to flames has inured your lungs and eyes to smoke. You can breathe normally in areas of ash and smoke without risk of suffocation, and you ignore the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) condition from smoke. You need only a successful DC 10 flat check to recover from [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29), rather than DC 15 (and the DC when receiving particularly effective assistance is 5 instead of 10).
