<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Firebrand Braggart Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1067) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
<trait label="Misfortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=110" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 74

**Archetype** [Firebrand Braggart](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=24)

**Prerequisites**
Charisma 14; second mark member of the Firebrands

</column>

---

Your Firebrand training has taught you that achieving something is more satisfying if you boast about it first. You declare a boast about a particular skill action, such as [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28), [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53), or [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26). The first time you attempt this action within the next minute in a context the GM deems both suitably challenging and meaningful, you must roll twice and use the lower result. If you succeed at this check, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks to attempt the same action for 10 minutes. If you fail this check or don’t attempt the action within 1 minute, you instead take a –1 circumstance penalty on checks to attempt the same action for 1 hour.

 If the chosen action can be used with multiple skills, such as [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24) or Recall Knowledge, you must specify which skill you are using for that particular action, such as using [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) to Identify Magic, and your bonus or penalty after the boast applies only to checks using that skill for that action. Once you declare a boast about a particular action, you cannot declare a boast about the same action until the next time you make daily preparations, regardless of whether you succeed or fail at the check.

 Typically a challenging task is one with at least a standard DC for your level, though the difficulty may be higher depending on the situation. A meaningful context is one where the action’s success or failure is relevant to the pursuit of your goals, rather than a boast you made simply to gain a bonus later.

**Special** You can’t select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Firebrand Braggart archetype.

<title level="2">Firebrand Braggart Dedication leads to...</title>
[Boaster's Challenge](/Feats.aspx?ID=1068), [Bravo's Determination](/Feats.aspx?ID=1070), [Daring Act](/Feats.aspx?ID=1069), [Great Boaster](/Feats.aspx?ID=1071)

**There is a more recent version of this, [click here to view.](/Feats.aspx?ID=8528)** **Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 134, [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 134 **Archetype** [Firework Technician](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=119) **Prerequisites** Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) --- You've learned the secrets of making fire and sound bloom using black powder, metals, and paper. You most likely came by this knowledge through formal training with a fireworks house in Tian Xia or a fireworks company from Vudra, though perhaps you mastered fireworks completely by yourself after finding a secret stash in an old shipwreck. You become trained in Fireworks Lore or become an expert if you were already trained in it. You gain the Alchemical Crafting feat, the [advanced alchemy benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=3282), and the [Quick Alchemy benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=3282), creating up to 4 versatile vials during your daily preparations. You can replenish these vials during exploration just like an alchemist can. You can use your versatile vials to make fireworks, Launch a Fireworks Display, and use other feats from this archetype (see below). You can also create a special item called a fireworks display using your daily alchemical consumables from your advanced alchemy benefits. These displays are designed to create distinctive effects you can use to make onlookers marvel and even to gain an advantage in combat. You gain the Launch Fireworks action and learn some basic effects. You can learn additional, more complex displays that use your daily fireworks display resources through other firework technician feats. The DC for any display is equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. **Launch Fireworks** to (see below); ([manipulate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2229)) **Cost** 1 versatile vial; **Requirements** You have a free hand; **Effect** You set off a fireworks display. You can launch a normal firework to simply create a visual or audible signal within 20 feet or you can choose one of the following special effects. A firework display has the listed traits, and if it costs more than 1 batch of infused reagents, it is noted in its Cost entry.
**Comet** ([visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) You shoot a streak of shining light in a 60-foot line. All spaces in that line are lit with [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2401) until the start of your next turn. As part of this action, you can also [Point Out](/Actions.aspx?ID=2315) a single creature in the line, and your allies do not need to hear or understand you.
**Flower** ([visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) You ignite a ring of sparks, creating a shape that might be reminiscent of a flower blooming in the sky. Each enemy with 20 feet of you must attempt a Fortitude save. On a failure, the enemy is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 round, and on a critical failure they are dazzled for 2 rounds.
**Salute** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541)) You create a startling bang or whistle, adding an auditory component to your fireworks display. When you launch a salute display, you can choose a [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) or [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) ally within 60 feet. If the ally you chose is fascinated, the noise is so violent that it acts as a hostile effect for the purpose of their fascinated condition (though it has no negative repercussions) automatically ending most applications of the fascinated condition. If they're confused, the sound is so loud and violent that it might snap the ally out of confusion. They can immediately attempt the flat check to remove the confused condition which normally occurs when a creature is damaged. If the confused condition has special rules that remove the flat check when taking damage or make the flat check harder, those rules also apply to the salute. Firework Technician Dedication leads to... [Banshee Cry Display](/Feats.aspx?ID=3250), [Coughing Dragon Display](/Feats.aspx?ID=3246), [Expert Fireworks Crafter](/Feats.aspx?ID=3247), [Goblin Jubilee Display](/Feats.aspx?ID=3249), [Jumping Jenny Display](/Feats.aspx?ID=3248)

  **Launch Fireworks** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Cost** 1 versatile vial; **Requirements** You're holding or wearing an alchemist's toolkit and have a free hand; **Effect** You set off a fireworks display. Each enemy in a 20-foot emanation must attempt a Fortitude save. On a failure, the enemy is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 round, and on a critical failure they are dazzled for 2 rounds.

  **Salute** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541)) You create a startling bang or whistle. When you launch a salute display, you can choose a [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) or [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) ally within 60 feet. If the ally you chose is fascinated, the noise is so violent that it acts as a hostile effect for the purpose of their fascinated condition (though it has no negative repercussions) automatically ending most applications of the fascinated condition. If they're confused, the sound is so loud and violent that it might snap the ally out of confusion. They can immediately attempt the flat check to remove the confused condition which normally occurs when a creature is damaged. If the confused condition has special rules that remove the flat check when taking damage or make the flat check harder, those rules also apply to the salute.

**Special** If you have Quick Alchemy from another source (such as the alchemist class or multiclass archetype), you can use standard versatile vials to Launch Fireworks or create fireworks consumables. Each time you create a versatile vial, you choose whether it's a standard vial or pyrotechnic vial. Both types count toward your maximum number of versatile vials. You can replenish only pyrotechnic vials during exploration unless another ability lets you replenish standard versatile vials (such as the benefit of the alchemist class), in which case you can choose the type each time you replenish.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 134

**Archetype** [Firework Technican](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=366)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

You’ve learned the secrets of making fire and sound bloom using black powder, metals, and paper. You most likely came by this knowledge through formal training with a fireworks house in Tian Xia or a fireworks company from Vudra, though perhaps you mastered fireworks completely by yourself after finding a secret stash in an old shipwreck.

You become trained in [Fireworks Lore](/Traits.aspx?ID=695) or become an expert if you were already trained in it. You gain the [Alchemical Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=5117) feat, a pool of infused reagents equal to your level, and advanced alchemy (allowing you to make alchemical items during your daily preparations without the normal cost or time expenditure). You can use your infused reagents only to make fireworks, Launch a Fireworks Display, and use other feats from this archetype (see below). Your advanced alchemy level is 1. The rules for these are in the [Alchemical Crafting](/Rules.aspx?ID=2634) section on page 258 of the Core Rulebook, and rules for infused reagents and [advanced alchemy are here](/Feats.aspx?ID=6185). If you gain infused reagents from more than one source, you use the highest number of reagents to determine your pool rather than adding them together.

You can also create special fireworks displays using your infused reagents, designed to create distinctive effects you can use to make onlookers marvel and even to gain an advantage in combat. You gain the Launch Fireworks Display action and learn some basic displays, and you can learn additional, more complex displays through other firework technician feats. The DC for any display is equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.

**Launch Fireworks Display** <actions string="Single Action" /> to <actions string="Three Actions" /> (see below); ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)); Cost 1 or more batches of infused reagents; **Requirements** You have a free hand; **Effect** You set off a fireworks display. You can launch a normal firework to simply create a visual or audible signal within 20 feet or you can choose one of the following special effects. A firework display has the listed traits, and if it costs more than 1 batch of infused reagents, it is noted in its Cost entry.

**Comet** <actions string="Single Action" /> (visual) You shoot a streak of shining light in a 60-foot [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388). All spaces in that line are lit with bright light until the start of your next turn. As part of this action, you can also [Point Out](/Actions.aspx?ID=2315) a single creature in the line, and your allies do not need to hear or understand you.

**Flower** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) You ignite a ring of sparks, creating a shape that might be reminiscent of a flower blooming in the sky. Each enemy with 20 feet of you must attempt a Fortitude save. On a failure, the enemy is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 round, and on a critical failure they are dazzled for 2 rounds.

**Salute** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541)) You create a startling bang or whistle, adding an auditory component to your fireworks display. When you launch a salute display, you can choose a [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) or [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) ally within 60 feet. If the ally you chose is fascinated, the noise is so violent that it acts as a hostile effect for the purpose of their fascinated condition (though it has no negative repercussions) automatically ending most applications of the fascinated condition. If they’re confused, the sound is so loud and violent that it might snap the ally out of confusion. They can immediately attempt the [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) to remove the confused condition which normally occurs when a creature is damaged. If the confused condition has special rules that remove the flat check when taking damage or make the flat check harder, those rules also apply to the salute.

**Special** You can’t select another dedication feat until you’ve gained two other feats from the fireworks technician archetype.

<title level="2">Firework Technician Dedication leads to...</title>
[Coughing Dragon Display](/Feats.aspx?ID=8751), [Expert Fireworks Crafter](/Feats.aspx?ID=8752), [Goblin Jubilee Display](/Feats.aspx?ID=8754), [Jumping Jenny Display](/Feats.aspx?ID=8753)

<traits>

<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=623" />
<trait label="Vitality" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=509" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 38

**Frequency**
once per day

**Trigger**
A living creature within 30 feet would die.

**Requirements**
Your divine spark is empowering one of your ikons.

</column>

---

Seeing your ally fall, you let out a cry, sending your divine spark to them temporarily to keep them from tumbling down the River of Souls. You prevent the triggering creature from dying and restore 5d8 Hit Points to them. The ally is invigorated by the touch of your divine power, gaining a +1 status bonus to their saving throws and AC for 1 round. Your divine spark remains with your ally, preventing you from gaining any of your ikons’ immanence effects until the start of your next turn, when it returns to an ikon of your choice.

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 38

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Kijimuna Gnome](/Heritages.aspx?ID=372) heritage

</column>

---

You can gain the magic of the seas by eating your favorite seafood. This gives you an advantage when diving, escaping notice after pilfering a valuable artifact from a local warlord, moving through poisonous fumes, or sleeping next to a particularly gassy adventuring partner. If you eat the left eye of a fish, you gain the [Breath Control](/Feats.aspx?ID=5129) feat for the next hour, and that feat’s benefits apply against effects that have the [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664) trait in addition to those that have the [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=634) 38 trait. As this feat is temporary, you can’t use it as a prerequisite for a permanent character option like a feat or access to a spell.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 90

**Archetype** [Five-breath Vanguard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=272)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Induce Imbalance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7013)

**Requirements**
You're in an elemental stance, and the target is under the effects of Induce Imbalance.

</column>

---

You cycle through the elements in a devastating combination attack. [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) the target using the unarmed attack associated with your current elemental stance, then Cycle Elemental Stance. Then, Strike the target with the unarmed attack associated with your new elemental stance. You can continue to Cycle Elemental Stance and Strike until you’ve made a Strike using the unarmed attack of every elemental stance you know, applying the multiple attack penalty as usual. If you successfully hit the target with all five elemental Strikes using this ability, it must attempt a Fortitude save against your class DC or die as each elementally associated organ within its body shuts down; this is a [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effect.

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Flamboyant Cruelty](/Feats.aspx?ID=2161) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=321" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 28

</column>

---

You love to kick your enemies when they're down, and you look fabulous when you do. When you make a melee weapon Strike against a foe that has at least two of the following conditions, you gain a circumstance bonus to your damage roll equal to the number of these conditions the foe has. The qualifying conditions are [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34), and [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37). If you hit such a foe, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to skill checks to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=29) and to perform your style's panache-granting actions until the end of your turn.

<title level="2">The General's Armory</title>

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 28

Azaersi believes in rewarding loyalty and service, and she is always in search of reliable and trustworthy agents. Sensible officers, clever spies, and trade negotiators who show skill at dealing with non-hobgoblins are all likely to win General Azaersi's favor, and rewards that only she can offer.

**Related Feats**: [Azaersi's Roads](/Feats.aspx?ID=2160)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Flamboyant Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=1550) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=321" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 92

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3); [Flamboyant Athlete](/Feats.aspx?ID=1527)

**Requirements**
You are capable of using a finisher.

</column>

---

You stylishly leap and deliver a powerful finisher. Make a [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36), or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37) and attempt one single-action finisher at any point during your jump; the finisher can't be one that includes other movement, such as Mobile Finisher. Immediately after the finisher, you fall to the ground if you're in the air, even if you haven't reached the maximum distance of your jump. If the distance you fall is no more than the height of your jump, you take no damage and land upright. When attempting a High Jump or Long Jump during a Flamboyant Leap, determine the DC using the Long Jump DCs, and increase the maximum distance to double your Speed, rather than just your Speed.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=66" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 11

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Emberkin](/Feats.aspx?ID=2283)

</column>

---

Your [peri](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1262) lineage has opened your mind to fire's raw, purging essence. You can spend 1 minute in focused preparation, then enter a fire your size or larger to instantly teleport to any fire that is your size or larger up to 5 miles away. You take no damage from entering or exiting fires when using this ability. Once you enter the fire, you instantly know the rough locations of other large fires within range and can exit from the original fire, if you prefer. You can't carry [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) spaces with you when you teleport; if you attempt to do so, the activity fails.

>
[Flames of Vision](/Feats.aspx?ID=6831) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Goblin" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=618" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 35

**Access**
dokkaebi goblin heritage or Tian Xia origin

</column>

---

Dokkaebi were among the first goblins to pioneer gazing through flames, spectral or physical, to cast their senses far and wide. You can cast [_clairvoyance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1466) as a 4th rank innate occult spell twice per day. To see through the spell’s eye, you must be staring into a source of fire.

**Special** If you can cast [_ignition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1565), including from the [Dokkaebi Fire](/Feats.aspx?ID=6516) feat, then you can cast that spell as part of casting clairvoyance. Instead of the cantrip’s normal effect, you conjure flames in your hand, which persist for the duration of your clairvoyance spell for you to gaze through.

An artificial metal object forms in the hands of you or a willing ally within 30 feet. You can choose a level 0, common, handheld [weapon](/Weapons.aspx) or piece of [adventuring gear](/Equipment.aspx?Category=1) of 1 Bulk or less. The item is entirely made from metal, making some items impossible or impractical to use (if it's unclear, the GM decides). You can make items with simple moving parts or magnetism, like a compass, poor lock, or merchant's scale. The item lasts for 10 minutes, but each time it's used, the user must succeed at a DC 5 flat check or the item is destroyed after the action is completed.

</traits>

**Prerequisites**

---

You make a fearsome show of your authority. Roll Intimidation checks to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) each creature in a 30-foot cone. When you do so, Demoralize gains the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) trait, and creatures are affected if they can see you. If a target creature hasn't broken a law in the past week (as determined by the GM), the result of your check against that creature is one degree of success worse than the result you rolled.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Flashy Roll](/Feats.aspx?ID=6159) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=825" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 167

**Prerequisites**
[Flashy Dodge](/Feats.aspx?ID=6129)

</column>

---

You can use Flashy Dodge before attempting a Reflex save, in addition to its original trigger. If you do, the circumstance bonus applies to your Reflex save against the triggering effect. 

When you use Flashy Dodge and the triggering attack fails or critically fails, or when you succeed or critically succeed at the saving throw, you can also Stride up to 10 feet as part of the reaction. If you do, the reaction gains the move trait. You can use Flashy Roll while [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) or [Swimming](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

[Flensing Slice](/Feats.aspx?ID=1953) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 170

**Archetype** [Dual-Weapon Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=57)

**Prerequisites**
[Dual-Weapon Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1950)

**Requirements**
Your last action was a [Double Slice](/Feats.aspx?ID=356), and both attacks hit the target.

</column>

---

When you hit with both attacks with Double Slice, you flense the target, making it bleed and creating a weak spot. The target takes 1d8 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) per weapon damage die of whichever of the weapons you used that has the most weapon damage dice (maximum 4d8 for a [_major striking_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) weapon). The target becomes [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16), and its resistances to any physical damage types are reduced by 5; these two effects last until the beginning of your next turn.

The altered ability loses the force trait and gains the trait of the new damage type.

>
[Fling Into action](/Feats.aspx?ID=7286) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 82

</column>

---

You release mythic power to turn disaster into opportunity and hurl yourself into an advantageous position. When you attempt a Reflex save, you can spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) to attempt the save at mythic proficiency. If the check is successful, you immediately fling yourself up to 30 feet in a direction of your choice, or up to 60 feet on a critical success. When flinging yourself in this manner, you can move the entire distance in a straight horizontal or vertical line, or you can move 5 feet horizontally for every 10 feet you move vertically. For example, if you got a critical success using Fling Into Action while [Grabbing an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2313) as you fall from the middle of a cliff, you could hurl yourself 40 feet up the cliffside and 20 feet forward onto a plateau at the top of the cliff.

You take a moment to center yourself, then unleash a powerful blow that sends your target tumbling away. Make an unarmed Strike. If you hit, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or be pushed up to 10 feet directly away from you (or 20 feet, on a critical failure) and fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). If another creature or physical object would prevent this movement, both your target and the blocking creature or object take 1d6 bludgeoning damage per 5 feet of movement that was prevented.

If the target doesn't land on a space of solid ground within 30 feet of where it started, it falls unless it has a fly Speed but doesn't take any damage from the fall.     level="1"
    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Flock As One](/Feats.aspx?ID=9477) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=670" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=676" />
<trait label="Strix" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=884" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 43

**Frequency**
once per week

</column>

---

Calling up deep primal magic, you and a small chosen few are remade into a flock of small birds. In a ceremony that takes 10 minutes to perform, you and up to 5 willing creatures within 15 feet of you are transformed into Tiny birds whose feathers resemble your own. They remain in this form for 8 hours, but an individual target can use the Sustain action to resume its normal shape or return to its bird form. While in this bird form, a target has a land Speed of 15 feet and a fly Speed of 40 feet; in exploration mode, a target can travel 20 miles per hour. A transformed target can’t Strike, cast spells, or use most manipulate actions.

>
[Flood Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7492) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=656" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=732" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 80

</column>

---

The lessons of the flood teach a stance that distributes and circulates a single breath through the body and allows your punches to contain the focused power of a torrent of water. While in this stance, you [hold your breath](/Rules.aspx?ID=2439) for up to 10 minutes and leave the stance if you stop holding your breath. You do not lose additional air if you attack, are critically hit, or critically fail a save. You still lose all remaining air if you speak, including to Cast a Spell. The only Strikes you can make are flooded river unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 bludgeoning damage; are in the brawling group; have the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661), [trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=716), [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719), and [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) traits; and don’t take the normal penalty for being used underwater. They also gain the forceful trait while you’re underwater.

<title level="2">Flood Stance leads to...</title>
[Culvert's Collapse](/Feats.aspx?ID=7498)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=583" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Vitality" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=509" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 132

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[leaf order](/DruidicOrders.aspx?ID=2)

</column>

---

You request that nearby plants share their vitality with you to replenish your body and magic. You regain 1 Focus Point and 4d8 Hit Points.

You must be in a location of at least 15 feet by 15 feet of healthy plant life, though this can be grass, lichen, seaweed, or any other form of naturally occurring flora. Using Floral Restoration on a given section of nature does not harm it, but it prevents that section of nature from giving its vitality to another use of Floral Restoration for 24 hours.

At 9th level, and every 2 levels thereafter, increase the healing by 1d8.

fields.text: Feat 11 Flower Street Infamy Single Action Uncommon Archetype Auditory Concentrate Linguistic Mental Skill Source Hellfire Dispatches pg. 47 Archetype Dandy Prerequisites Dandy Dedication Your history of coquetries, flirtations, dalliances, and liaisons is so lengthy that, even in a city as large as Absalom, you're bound to run into your past at inopportune moments. Fortunately, the individual involved might be just as shocked as you are by the unexpected encounter. Choose a target within 30 feet and spin a lascivious tale of how the two of you might have met before. Attempt a Deception check against the target's Will DC. Regardless of your result, the target is temporarily immune to your Flower Street Infamy for 24 hours. Critical Success The target is stupefied 3 for 1 minute. Success The target is stupefied 2 for 1 minute. Failure The target is stupefied 1 until the start of your next turn. Critical Failure The target is unaffected.

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Flying Kick](/Feats.aspx?ID=5993) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=656" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 121

</column>

---

You launch yourself at a foe. Make a [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) or attempt a [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378). At the end of the jump, if you're adjacent to a foe, you can immediately Strike that foe with an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) attack, even if the foe is in midair. You fall to the ground after the Strike. If the distance you fall is no more than the height of your jump, you land upright and take no damage.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Flying Tackle](/Feats.aspx?ID=7847) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
<trait label="Guardian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=859" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 43

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36)

</column>

---

You barrel forward, gathering enough momentum to take down a threatening foe. Stride and then [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298), or attempt to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378). If you end your movement adjacent to a foe, you can attempt to Trip that foe. If you succeed at the Athletics check to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382), you get a critical success instead. You can use Flying Tackle while Burrowing, Climbing, Flying, or Swimming instead of Striding if you have the corresponding  movement type.

fields.text: Feat 7 Foil Senses General Skill Source Core Rulebook pg. 261 Prerequisites Master in Stealth You are adept at foiling creatures' special senses and cautious enough to safeguard against them at all times. Whenever you use the Avoid Notice, Hide, or Sneak actions, you are always considered to be taking precautions against special senses (see the Detecting with Other Senses sidebar).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Folk Dowsing](/Feats.aspx?ID=3774) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 78

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

You can find what you're looking for using a dowsing rod or pendulum. If you [Search](/Actions.aspx?ID=519) while wielding a dowsing rod or pendulum, in addition to the normal checks for Searching, the GM rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) check for you to detect the largest source of water, oil, or another natural non-bodily fluid in the area. Even if the liquid is concealed from you—for example, if it stems from an underground spring or is piped through a wall—this technique points you in the right direction. The GM determines the DC, which is usually the [trained simple DC](/Rules.aspx?ID=553) with a [hard or very hard adjustment](/Rules.aspx?ID=555) if the source of water is small.

 If you're an expert in Survival, the GM also makes a Survival check for you to detect sizable deposits of metal, minerals, and nearby graves. The DC is usually the expert simple DC, with DC adjustments for smaller deposits.

    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Folk Healer](/Feats.aspx?ID=6914) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Sarangay" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=829" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 61

</column>

---

Your community recognizes you as a shaman or other animist, a status you obtained through lineage, apprenticeship, or a supernatural event. You’re trained in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) and [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44). If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Medicine checks to [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399) and [Treat Disease](/Actions.aspx?ID=2397).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Folklorist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3034) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind](/Sources.aspx?ID=97) pg. 78

**Archetype** [Folklorist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=105)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12)

</column>

---

You are a master archivist and entertainer, capable of pulling wisdom from the tales you tell and weaving your allies and enemies into a powerful narrative. You gain the Spin Tale action. 

**Spin Tale** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101)) **Frequency** once every 10 minutes; **Effect** You tell a story, designating one of your allies (but not yourself) as the hero of the story, and one enemy as the villain; both must be within 60 feet. The hero gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls and saving throws against the villain until the start of your next turn. If you Spin a Tale on your next turn, the story continues for another round, for a maximum of 10 rounds. While the tale continues, minor, crude illusions spring into being in your space; these are [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11) [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92) effects that have no mechanical impact other than illustrating your tale.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the folklorist archetype.

<title level="2">Folklorist Dedication leads to...</title>
[Communal Tale](/Feats.aspx?ID=3038), [Folktales Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=3035), [Narrative Conduit](/Feats.aspx?ID=3036), [Rule of Three](/Feats.aspx?ID=3037)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Folksy Patter](/Feats.aspx?ID=1430) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Halfling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=87" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 46

</column>

---

You are adept at disguising coded messages as folksy idioms. Using slang, jokes, halfling loanwords, and the like, you convey a simple message consisting of three basic words (such as “Danger assassin flee” or “Meet me moonrise”). Your intended listener can attempt a Perception check to discern the message (DC 20 if an ally, DC 15 if a halfling ally, DC 10 if a halfling ally with Folksy Patter). Eavesdroppers can also attempt a Perception check against your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) DC to discern your meaning. Any bonuses or penalties to Perception checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85) apply.

[Folktales Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=3035) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind](/Sources.aspx?ID=97) pg. 78

**Archetype** [Folklorist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=105)

**Prerequisites**
[Folklorist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3034)

</column>

---

You can pull bits of wisdom from any tale. You become trained in Folktales Lore, a special [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill that can be used only to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26), but on any topic. If you fail a check to Recall Knowledge with Folktales Lore, you get the effects of the [Dubious Knowledge](/Feats.aspx?ID=776) skill feat.

 If you are legendary in the Performance skill, you gain expert proficiency in Folktales Lore, but you can't increase your proficiency rank in Folktales Lore by any other means.

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Follow the Threads of Fate](/Feats.aspx?ID=8008) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=76" />
<trait label="Ikon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=840" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #217: Death Sails a Wine-Dark Sea
](/Sources.aspx?ID=273) pg. 79

**Usage**
imbued into a worn [ikon](/Ikons.aspx) made of cloth or a weapon ikon with a tassel, wrapping, or similar feature.

</column>

---

A [norn’s](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=448) thread—spun from fate itself—runs through or wraps around your ikon. 

**Transcendence—Unravel the Future** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612), [transcendence](/Traits.aspx?ID=842)) You pluck a single thread from your ikon, which ties itself in three loops about your wrist, where it remains for the next minute. If you fail an attack roll or skill check, and a +1 status bonus would change your failure into a success or your success into a critical success, you gain a +1 status bonus to this check retroactively, changing the outcome appropriately as the thread pulls you to the future you desire. The thread then falls from your wrist. You can have only one thread in existence at a time.

Your techniques extend the storage life for certain ingredients and food through pickling, alcohol, or fermentation. When you use [advanced alchemy](/Feats.aspx?ID=6185) to create alchemical food, you can designate one infused item to not automatically expire when you next make your daily preparations. When you preserve another item in this way, the previous item becomes inedible. 

The number of items you can preserve during your daily preparation and the maximum number of items you can have preserved before spoiling older items increases to two if you’re an expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) or Cooking [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41), to three if you’re a master, and to five if you’re legendary.

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 44 **Archetype** [Scrollmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=31) **Prerequisites** [Scrollmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1130) --- You feel confident that you can explain your scrolls so well that even your allies can use them... hopefully. During your daily preparations, you can select a single scroll and instruct a single ally in its use. Until your next daily preparations, the ally can attempt to use the scroll with a single action that has the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) trait. The ally rolls the skill corresponding to the spellcasting tradition. The GM determines the DC based on the scroll's level, possibly adjusted for the situation. If the spell has a spell attack bonus or a spell DC, use your level as the proficiency bonus and the highest of your ally's Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifiers. **Success** For the rest of the ally's turn, they can spend actions to Cast the Spell.
**Failure** The ally misremembers your instructions and can't use the scroll this turn.
**Critical Failure** The ally misunderstood your instructions and can't use the scroll.

You learn the [_for love, for lightning_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1108) focus spell. If you don't already have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can regain using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) activity to recite the Crimson Oath and meditate on its teachings; if you already have a focus pool, increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1. Charisma is the key spellcasting ability for knight reclaimant focus spells.

---

While using Survival to Subsist, if you roll any result worse than a success, you get a success. On a success, you can provide subsistence living for yourself and four additional creatures, and on a critical success, you can take care of twice as many additional creatures. You can choose to support half the number of creatures with a comfortable living.

Increase the number of additional creatures you feed on a success to eight if you’re an expert in Survival, 16 if you’re a master, and 32 if you’re legendary.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Forager](/Feats.aspx?ID=786) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 261

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

While using Survival to Subsist, if you roll any result worse than a success, you get a success. On a success, you can provide subsistence living for yourself and four additional creatures, and on a critical success, you can take care of twice as many creatures as on a success.

 Each time your proficiency rank in Survival increases, double the number of additional creatures you can take care of on a success (to eight if you’re an expert, 16 if you’re a master, or 32 if you’re legendary). You can choose to care for half the number of additional creatures and provide a comfortable living instead of subsistence living.

 Multiple smaller creatures or creatures with significantly smaller appetites than a human are counted as a single creature for this feat, and larger creatures or those with significantly greater appetites each count as multiple creatures. The GM determines how much a non-human creature needs to eat.

<title

    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Forcible Energy](/Feats.aspx?ID=1841) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Metamagic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=107" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 143

</column>

---

You perform complex manipulations to make the energy from your spells so powerful that your enemies remain vulnerable to it afterward. If your next action is to Cast a Spell that deals acid, electricity, fire, or sonic damage, you can select one target that was damaged to gain weakness 5 to that damage type until the end of your next turn. If a spell deals multiple types of energy damage, choose one that the target gains weakness to. This has no effect on creatures with resistance or immunity to the energy type you choose.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Forensic Acumen](/Feats.aspx?ID=2128) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 206

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9)

</column>

---

You understand the principles of forensic medicine, making you better at examining a body to determine the cause of death or injury. You can perform a forensic examination on a body, as described under [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) in the [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) skill, in half the normal amount of time it would take (to a minimum of 5 minutes). If you succeed at your check, you can attempt an immediate check to Recall Knowledge to follow up on something you found, with a +2 circumstance bonus. This check is usually related to the cause of injury or death, such as a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) check to identify a poison or weapon that was used or an additional Medicine check to identify a specific disease. If you prefer, you can instead attempt to Recall Knowledge about the type of creature whose body you were examining, using the appropriate skill and gaining the same circumstance bonus.

 The circumstance bonus increases to +3 if you have master proficiency in Medicine and +4 if you have legendary proficiency.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Forensic Countermeasures](/Feats.aspx?ID=9012) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=318" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 65

**Prerequisites**
[empiricism methodology](/Methodologies.aspx?ID=6)

**Access**
member of the Red Mantis assassins

</column>

---

Your knowledge of deductive reasoning allows you to derail fellow [investigators](/Classes.aspx?ID=59). Over the course of a minute, you can tamper with a single location (such as a small room) to either obscure evidence or add misleading evidence. If you add misleading evidence, you choose what incorrect details it implies. A creature can see through these countermeasures with a successful [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) check against your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) DC, and only if they actively look for tampering.

If you add misleading evidence, you choose what incorrect details it implies. A creature can see through these countermeasures with a successful Recall Knowledge check against your Deception DC, and only if they actively look for tampering.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Foresee Danger](/Feats.aspx?ID=1471) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=318" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 64

**Trigger**
A creature targets you with an attack and you can see the attacker.

</column>

---

You perceive every possible way your foe's attack could land and attempt to avoid them all. The triggering attack roll targets your Perception DC instead of your AC. Though this allows you to avoid taking penalties to your AC, it doesn't remove any conditions or other effects causing such penalties. For example, an enemy with sneak attack would still deal extra damage to you for being [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16), even though you wouldn't take the –2 circumstance penalty when defending against the attack.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=76" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 28

**Frequency**
once per day

**Trigger**
A spell you cast has no effect because you critically failed all your spell attack rolls or because all targets critically succeeded at their saving throws.

</column>

---

You see your spell fail to take hold to disastrous end, then snap back to reality—it was all a precognition, and you know to try a different spell. Your spell is expended, but you can Cast a Spell that requires the same number of actions as the triggering spell or fewer to cast. The second spell must be a different spell than the first.

    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Forest's Heart](/Feats.aspx?ID=7146) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Animist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=836" />
<trait label="Apparition" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=837" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
<trait label="Wandering" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=843" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 26

**Requirements**
Your attuned apparition grants Forest [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) or Herbalism Lore as one of its apparition skills.

</column>

---

You adopt a stance that allows your apparitions to channel spiritual energy down through you to inhabit roots, control vines, and command plant-life from the ground you stand on to fight on your behalf. You call forth roots, vines, or other plant growth native to the region and can use them to make unarmed attacks. These deal 4d8 bludgeoning damage, are in the [brawling group](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4), and have the [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [grapple](/Traits.aspx?ID=619), and [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=684) 30 feet traits. Attacks made with these unarmed attacks don’t gain additional damage from [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) runes, but can benefit from the item bonus to attack rolls and [property runes](/Rules.aspx?ID=3168) of [handwraps of mighty blows](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3086) you wear.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cursebound" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=800" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=817" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 138

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The oracle's Foretell Harm feat can be used on all targets of an area-of-effect spell, not just a singular target._

**Frequency**
once per round

**Requirements**
Your previous action was to [Cast](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) a non-cantrip Spell that dealt damage

</column>

---

Your magic echoes ominously as you glimpse injury in the target's future. At the beginning of your target's next turn, it takes damage equal to twice the triggering spell's rank as a seemingly random and minor misfortune finds it. The damage and type of misfortune is of a type matching the spell; for instance, if you dealt fire damage, a flame might spontaneous ignite on them or they might burn a hand on their torch. The target is then temporarily immune to Foretell Harm for 24 hours.

**Frequency**
once per minute

**Prerequisites**
[Overwatch Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3118); master in Perception

**Trigger**
An enemy within your overwatch field attempts an attack against an ally who is also within your overwatch field.

</column>

---

Your foresight and planning are more valuable than armor as you direct your ally away from danger, but there's a limit to how often you can guide your allies away from a foe's relentless assaults. The triggering attack roll targets your Perception DC instead of your ally's AC. Though this allows your ally to avoid taking penalties to their AC, it doesn't remove any conditions or other effects causing such penalties. For example, an enemy with sneak attack would still deal extra damage to your ally if they are [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16), even though they wouldn't take the –2 circumstance penalty when defending against the attack.

[Forge New Word](/Feats.aspx?ID=9217) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 53

</column>

---

At the pinnacle of your art, you have forged a new great rune of power, a new ideal expression or utterance to be added to the craft. You create a rune and add it to your runic repertoire. When you gain this feat, choose a spell of 4th rank or lower. It must be common, or you must otherwise have access to it. The spell must take 1 or 2 actions to cast. You can choose a variable action spell, deciding when you create the rune whether the rune uses the 1-action or 2-action version of the spell. Name your rune. This rune has the [unique](/Traits.aspx?ID=723) trait and a [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) trait of your choosing ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)). 

This rune can be drawn on a creature or object, regardless of what the spell can target. When invoked, this rune has the effect of the chosen spell. The rune-bearer is the point of origin for the spell’s effect; calculate range and cover from its space. If the spell has targets, you decide who or what the spell targets, and the rune-bearer is a possible target if your chosen spell can target it. If the spell can affect only you (such as [_translocate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724)), invoking it affects only you, and has no effect if the rune is drawn anywhere other than on you. If the spell requires a spell attack roll, use your class DC – 10 in place of the spell attack modifier. If your chosen spell has a duration and that duration is longer than 1 minute, the invoked rune’s duration is 1 minute instead.

You intone a prayer to the dwarven deities Torag or Angradd, willing a higher power to guide your aim in the heat of battle. <column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 213

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

You call nearby wild dragonets to swarm to your side. The flock grants you 25 [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) that last up to 1 minute. The flock disperses and the effect ends when the temporary Hit Points are gone, the minute elapses, or you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) Form a Flock. As long as you’re surrounded by your flock, you gain [weakness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 5 to area and splash damage and have a flock aura in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). Enemies in this aura are [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65). 

When you use Form a Flock and while it lasts, you can take the Acrid Barrage action.

**Acrid Barrage** <actions string="Two Actions" /> **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** Each enemy in your aura takes 5d6 acid damage and 2d6 [persistent acid damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. The initial damage increases to 6d6 at 15th level and 7d6 at 18th level.

You channel the blessings of Nalinivati to transform into a manifestation of her will. You can cast 5th-rank animal form as an [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662) innate spell once per day, but you can choose only snake form with the spell. You can spend an additional action casting [_animal form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1440) to also cast 5th-rank [_slither_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1676) centered on your location; Nalinivati’s will ensures that the shadow snakes created by the spell never harm you, so you’re unaffected by the spell. If you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) animal form, the effects of slither end as well.

---

You have trained your mind and body to tolerate [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) magic for longer periods of time, so long as you prepare for the change appropriately. When preparing a polymorph spell that lasts 1 minute and grants a battle form, you can prepare the spell in a slot 2 levels higher than normal. This doesn't grant any of the normal benefits of heightening a spell, but the spell lasts up to 10 minutes. For example, if you prepared [_animal form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=10) in a 4th-level slot with Form Retention, you would cast a 2nd-level _animal form_ that lasts for up to 10 minutes. If the spell can be Dismissed, that doesn't change.

<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=735" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 203

---

You have trained your mind and body to tolerate polymorph magic for longer periods of time, so long as you prepare for the change appropriately. When preparing a polymorph spell that lasts 1 minute and grants a battle form, you can prepare the spell in a slot 2 ranks higher than normal. This doesn’t grant any of the normal benefits of heightening a spell, but the spell lasts up to 10 minutes. For example, if you prepared animal form in a 4th-rank slot with Form Retention, you would cast a 2nd-rank animal form that lasts for up to 10 minutes. If the spell can be Dismissed, that doesn’t change.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />

**Archetype** [Marshal](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=254)

**Prerequisites**
[Marshal Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6351)

</column>

---

You’ve trained in battle formations for a plethora of situations. Choose a formation. Allies within your aura can use their reaction to Stride up to their Speed and take a place in the chosen formation. Allies can’t benefit from this movement if there isn’t room for them in the chosen formation. If there are more eligible allies than there are available spaces in the chosen formation, you choose which allies benefit.

**Line** Your allies gather adjacent to you and each other to form a straight line in a direction of your choosing. 

**Wedge** Your allies gather into any space that would be covered by a 15-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) originating from you in a direction of your choosing. 

**Cluster** Your allies gather into any space that would be covered by a 15-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) in an aura around you.

You intone vows to shoulder others’ pains; in response, your torso sprouts an additional pair of arms to help you bear those burdens. For the following minute, you can carry 3 more Bulk than normal before becoming [encumbered](/Conditions.aspx?ID=70) and up to a maximum of 6 more Bulk. You can also use these arms as free hands to perform only the following actions or activities: [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=2383), [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376), [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380), and [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382). After this minute or when you become [unconscious](/Rules.aspx?ID=378), whichever comes first, these additional arms fade away.

Your reputation for transparency and fairness in conducting elections, appointments, and other changes in government inspires tremendous public trust. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Loyalty-based checks attempted as part of the [New Leadership](/Actions.aspx?ID=1378) and [Pledge of Fealty](/Actions.aspx?ID=1379) activities. You grow a nourishing nut, vegetable, seed, or fruit. Choose a creature in your kinetic aura. The produce grows in their open hand, or at their feet if they have no open hands. The produce has light Bulk. A creature can eat it with an Interact action to regain 1d4 + 1 HP; this is a healing vitality effect. The creature feels full for 10 minutes, during which it has resistance 2 to void damage and can't eat another piece of produce. Produce not consumed by the start of your next turn withers away.

---
**Level (+2)** The healing increases by 1d4+5, and the resistance increases by 2.

The shared bond between you and your allies allows you to act on their behalf. You lose access to a participant's form if they're not carrying your token or if you use the ritual again.

---

You can scoop up your friends with your horns to hurl them across the battlefield. Pick up an adjacent willing ally who is smaller than you and toss them to an unoccupied space you can see within 20 feet. Since you are using your horns, you don't need to have any hands free to do this. Your ally's movement doesn't trigger reactions. Your ally ends this movement on their feet and doesn't take damage from the fall but takes 1d6 piercing damage from your horns. If your ally ends this movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, they can make a melee Strike against an enemy within their reach as a reaction.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 29

**Archetype** [Undead Slayer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=174)

**Prerequisites**
[Undead Slayer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3474); Trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7)

</column>

---

Your very presence chills creatures of the night down to their core and you can use the spiritual power and faithful life force of religious verses to frighten even [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=108) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). Attempt to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) an undead target using your [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) modifier instead of your [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) modifier if it's higher. If you use your Religion modifier, the Demoralize action loses the [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60) and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) traits, as your faith connects to the undead on an instinctual level.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 21 **Frequency** once per day --- You have a connection to water and are able to call upon it to batter your foes and carry them away. You create a massive wave of water that crashes in a 20-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385) within 120 feet that moves in the direction of your choice. All creatures in the area take 14d6 bludgeoning damage and could be swept away. At the beginning of subsequent turns for 3 rounds, the wave moves 30 feet in the direction you chose; creatures in the area who aren’t already swept away by the wave take the bludgeoning damage. Creatures being swept away are trapped within the wave and can attempt to Escape against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, to end the effect. Otherwise, the creature remains swept away until the wave stops moving. The wave also extinguishes all non-magical fires in its path automatically. Creatures are affected based on the result of their Reflex saves with a DC equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage and is [moved](/Rules.aspx?ID=2364) 10 feet in the direction of the wave, but not swept away.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is fully swept away by the wave. The creature moves along with the wave until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296).
**Critical Failure** As failure, except the creature takes double damage and must hold its breath or begin [suffocating](/Rules.aspx?ID=2439) (unless it can breathe in water).

    right="Feat 12"

>
[Frostbite Runes](/Feats.aspx?ID=3417) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monsters of Myth](/Sources.aspx?ID=107) pg. 11

**Archetype** [Pactbound Initiate](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=167)

**Prerequisites**
[Pactbound Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3414)

</column>

---

Thick tattoos, each one a rune fragment from the saumen kar's long-lost language spelling out their pact with their equally lost deity, cover your body and stretch across your limbs, torso, and face. You gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against [evil](/Traits.aspx?ID=64) and [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117) spells and effects. You can sense the presence of evil [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) as a pervasive taste of oily corruption in the air; this is a [vague](/Rules.aspx?ID=413) sense that allows you to know when such a creature is within 60 feet of you, though you can't precisely pinpoint their location with this sense. As normal for a vague sense, it can be fooled, but undead might not realize they need to take precautions against it. This sense also extends to living creatures who have the [negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42) ability, like [dhampir](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=23).

 You deal an additional 1 cold damage with all Strikes made with an ice-crafted weapon. If you have the [Crown of the Saumen Kar](/Feats.aspx?ID=3416) feat, you deal an additional 1 cold damage with your unarmed horns Strikes.

<title level="2">Frostbite Runes leads to...</title>
[Bound in Ice](/Feats.aspx?ID=3419), [Curse of the Saumen Kar](/Feats.aspx?ID=3418)

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 32 **Prerequisites** [armor](/Innovations.aspx?ID=1), [construct](/Innovations.aspx?ID=2), or [weapon](/Innovations.aspx?ID=3) innovation --- You become so entwined with your innovations that you can use them without a second thought. You're permanently [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=32). How you can use the extra action depends on your innovation.
  • **Armor** Your armor responds to the most subtle stimuli to move you in the right direction as long as you are wearing it. You can use the extra action to Stride, Step, or use a form of movement provided by your innovation (such as [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39)).
  • **Construct** Your ability to command your construct becomes instinctive. You can use the extra action to Command your construct innovation (or to provide 1 of the actions if you choose to spend 2 actions to Command your construct).
  • **Weapon** Your weapon becomes easier to wield with deadly efficacy, almost as if it is an extension of your body. It speeds effortlessly toward whatever target you choose as long as you are holding it. You can use the extra action to Strike with your innovation.

fields.text: Feat 6 Fulu Familiar Archetype Talisman Source Tian Xia Character Guide pg. 116 Archetype Familiar Sage Prerequisites Familiar Sage Dedication; Expert in Occultism or Expert in Religion You can imprint your familiar’s spiritual essence into a fulu, a small paper charm that can be affixed to objects, creatures, or structures. You gain the Create Familiar Fulu action, which you can use once per day; at 12th level, this increases to twice per day, and at 18th level, it increases to three times per day. Action Create Familiar Fulu Two Actions Source Tian Xia Character Guide pg. 116 Frequency once per day or greater Requirements Your familiar is within 30 feet, and you have one hand free (concentrate, manipulate) You make a pinching motion, and your familiar dissolves into magical energy that re-forms between your fingers as a fulu magical item. The fulu must be at least two levels lower than your level, and you don’t need to spend the normal monetary cost in magical components or attempt a Crafting check. You can then choose to Affix a Talisman as part of this activity to affix your familiar fulu. While transformed, your familiar doesn’t grant its normal benefits, and it remains transformed until your next daily preparations or until you Activate the fulu, at which point your familiar reappears in an unoccupied space adjacent to you.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=127" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 29

---

Opening your kinetic gate, you allow flames to consume your form and leave you a living flame. You gain the benefits of the [_fiery body_](/Spells.aspx?ID=115) spell (except the ability to cast [_ignition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=236)) until the end of your next turn. You can Sustain the impulse up to 1 minute, and when you do, you can Fly up to half your fly Speed. Your fire [Elemental Blasts](/Actions.aspx?ID=2125) deal an additional die of damage.

---
**Level (16th)** This duration is 1 minute, you can't Sustain the impulse, and you can Dismiss the impulse.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=112" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 165

**Archetype** [Sister of the Golden Erinys](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=380) (Level 18)

**Prerequisites**
at least two [stances](/Traits.aspx?ID=152)

</column>

---

You have combined two stances into a single stance all your own. When you take this feat, choose two stances you know and combine them into a single fused stance. Give your new fused stance a unique name. When you enter your fused stance, you gain all the effects of both stances, including the requirements and restrictions.

 You can't fuse stances with fundamentally incompatible requirements or restrictions (such as [Mountain Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=435) and [Crane Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=430), which both require using only one type of Strike).

**Archetype** [Sister of the Golden Erinys](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=380) (Level 18)

at least two stances

</column>

---

You have combined two stances into a single stance all your own. When you take this feat, choose two stances you know and combine them into a single fused stance. Give your new fused stance a unique name. When you enter your fused stance, you gain all the effects of both stances, including the requirements and restrictions.

 If the stances both grant special attacks, you gain all those attacks. If a stance restricts you to one particular attack (such as [Crane Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=430)), you must abide by that restriction. If the fused stances have incompatible restrictions, the GM determines which apply, or determines you can't fuse those stances at all.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fused Polearm](/Feats.aspx?ID=3025) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 241

**Archetype** [Runelord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=103)

**Prerequisites**
[Runelord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3020)

**Requirements**
Your arcane bonded item is a [polearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=11).

</column>

---

During your daily preparations, you can magically fuse your arcane bonded weapon and a [magical staff](/Equipment.aspx?Category=32) together into one item, with the staff making up the haft of the weapon. You prepare the staff at the same time you do this, and you can do this only with a staff you're able to prepare. This fusion lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations. The staff and the weapon share their fundamental runes, using whichever weapon potency and whichever striking rune is higher level. They don’t share any other runes or specific abilities; use the polearm's.

While the two are fused, the weapon’s haft takes on aesthetic aspects of the staff, and it can't change forms, such as with the shifting rune.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fused Staff](/Feats.aspx?ID=2864) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 46

**Prerequisites**
[Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755)

</column>

---

When you prepare a [staff](/Equipment.aspx?Category=32), you can hold it up to a weapon to merge the two items. You can switch the fused item's form from the weapon to the staff or vice versa as a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait. When the item is in staff form, you can Cast the Spells from the staff and benefit from any other abilities the staff grants. The staff and the weapon share their fundamental runes, using whichever _[weapon potency](/Equipment.aspx?ID=281)_ and whichever _[striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280)_ rune is higher level. They don't share any other runes or specific abilities.

 You can Cast Spells from the staff as part of a Spellstrike even when the staff is in weapon form. Otherwise, you can't cast the staff's spells while it's in weapon form.

 The fusion lasts until your next daily preparations, though you can spend 10 minutes to separate the two items and meld the staff into a different weapon. The melding works for you alone. A different wielder can use the staff in its current form but can't transform it, get the benefit of the shared runes, or use its spells for a Spellstrike if it's in weapon form.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Fused Staff](/Feats.aspx?ID=9067) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=953" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 21

</column>

---

You can use your arcane prowess to fuse a magical staff into a weapon during your daily preparations or as a 10-minute activity with the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait. The fusion lasts until you fuse the staff again or the weapon is out of your possession for 24 hours. The fused item has the staff’s activations and other benefits, and it can be used to cast spells if you prepare it. The staff and the weapon share their [fundamental runes](/Rules.aspx?ID=3167), using whichever [_weapon potency_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) and whichever [_striking_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) rune is higher level. If the staff has [property runes](/Rules.aspx?ID=3168), they’re suppressed while it’s fused.

The item’s fused abilities work for you alone. A different wielder can use the weapon normally, but they don’t get the benefit of the shared runes and can’t use the staff’s spells or abilities.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Gadget Specialist](/Feats.aspx?ID=3058) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 26

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

Rather than just using your gadgets for various boosts and tweaks, you also craft a few specific temporary consumable gadgets each day. You gain the formulas for three common or uncommon [gadgets](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=71). Each day during your daily preparations, you can create two temporary gadgets from your formula book. Gadgets prepared in this way don't cost you any resources to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) and don't have any sale value. They are temporary items and fall apart the next time you make your daily preparations if you haven't already used them. 

If you're a master in Crafting, you can create three gadgets per day, and you gain three additional common or uncommon gadget formulas. If you're legendary in Crafting, you can create four gadgets per day, and you gain another additional three common or uncommon gadget formulas, for a total of nine.

<title level="2">Gadget Specialist leads to...</title>
[Contingency Gadgets](/Feats.aspx?ID=3074), [Ubiquitous Gadgets](/Feats.aspx?ID=3068)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 121

**Archetype** [Nidalese Horselord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=381)

**Prerequisites**
[Nidalese Horselord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8937)

</column>

---

Though your enemy wields shadow and darkness as weapons, they are no impediment to you when you ride your trusted horse. To that end, your mount can step onto patches of darkness as if they were solid. When your horse moves through an area of [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569), it can treat empty spaces as solid ground. This allows your horse to move across gaps bridged by darkness or even into the air, ascending or descending at a maximum of a 45-degree angle. If your horse isn't on actual solid ground and the area your horse is in becomes [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2401) or brighter, your horse falls.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 81

**Archetype** [Game Hunter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=169)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

You are skilled at tracking big game animals and similar creatures. You gain the [Hunt Prey](/Actions.aspx?ID=10) action, but you can designate only [animals](/Traits.aspx?ID=9), [beasts](/Traits.aspx?ID=20), and [dragons](/Traits.aspx?ID=50) as prey. In addition to the other benefits of Hunt Prey, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks against your hunted prey.

 When you succeed at a Strike against your hunted prey while it's [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16), it must attempt a Fortitude save against your class DC. On a failure, the prey's Speeds are each reduced by 10 feet for 1 round; on a critical failure, the duration of this effect is 1 minute. The prey is then temporarily immune to this effect for 10 minutes.

 If you already have Hunt Prey, you become an expert in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16). You apply the Stealth bonus and the Speed reduction only when your prey is an animal, beast, or dragon.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the game hunter archetype.

<title level="2">Game Hunter Dedication leads to...</title>
[Big Game Trapper](/Feats.aspx?ID=3426), [Keep Pace](/Feats.aspx?ID=3427), [Quick Positioning](/Feats.aspx?ID=3428)
