</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fleshwarp" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=338" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 92

**Frequency**
once per day

**Trigger**
A creature you are aware of damages you with a melee Strike.

</column>

---

Your wound yawns open, appalling your attacker. The attacker must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, or become [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) (sickened 2 on a critical failure). It can't recover from the sickened condition while it's adjacent to you.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Garland Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4750) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=583" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 133

**Prerequisites**
[leaf order](/DruidicOrders.aspx?ID=2)

</column>

---

If your next action is to Cast a Spell with the fungus or plant trait, a garland of plants grows in a 10-foot burst in the spell’s range. The plants are difficult terrain and hazardous terrain, covered in your choice of thorns or poisonous vines. Any creature that moves into one of these squares or ends its turn in one takes 2d6 damage (piercing damage for thorns or poison for vines). A creature can take this damage only once per turn. You and your familiar are immune to this damage.

The plants last for 1 minute or until you cast another Garland Spell, whichever comes first.

The damage increases to 3d6 at 16th level and 4d6 at 20th level.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Gather Disciples](/Feats.aspx?ID=8885) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 49

**Archetype** [Starstone Aspirant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=376)

**Prerequisites**
[Starstone Aspirant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8877); Master in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

</column>

---

Gods need followers, and you know that its best to gather a flock in the present to support you in your endeavor. Of course, you'll reward their faith in you in the future when you become a true deity. You can spend 1 week of downtime in a settlement to evangelize your coming godhood and establish a small group of disciples to your faith. Once this group has been established, these disciples are always helpful to you. You can use Religion to [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) something of them, though your request must be able to be performed by the type of people who would follow you, at the GM's discretion. If you critically succeed at this check, your disciples give a piece of helpful advice or let you in on a small secret, granting you or a member of your party a +2 circumstance bonus to the first skill check you attempt when acting on the favor. If you critically fail this check, your disciples' attitude toward you doesn't worsen.

 You can have three groups of disciples at any one time (or five if you're legendary in Religion). If you exceed this number, the oldest group disbands and must be established again if you return to that settlement.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 54

**Archetype** [Trapsmith](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=111)

**Prerequisites**
[Trapsmith Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3134); Expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

[Snares](/Equipment.aspx?Category=31) you create have complicated inner workings that are quite difficult to disable. Creatures attempting to [Disable](/Actions.aspx?ID=69) your snares that use gears must succeed at an additional [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) check in order to disable the snare. On a failed check, while the snare doesn't fully trigger, the grinding mechanisms deal bludgeoning damage to the creature equal to half your level. The snare still triggers on a critical failure, as normal.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Gear Up](/Feats.aspx?ID=3480) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 29

**Archetype** [Undead Slayer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=174)

**Prerequisites**
[Undead Slayer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3474)

</column>

---

Whether it's wooden stakes, holy water, or more unusual tools, you always have just the right thing to handle an [undead's](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) unusual weaknesses and vulnerabilities. You gain the [Prescient Planner](/Feats.aspx?ID=2143) and [Prescient Consumable](/Feats.aspx?ID=2142) feats. When using Prescient Planner specifically to pull out an item you need to deal with an undead's weakness or vulnerability, you can pull out the item as a 2-action activity to remove your backpack (or similar container) and draw the item, rather than taking 1 minute. If you have the Hunter's Sanctum feat, you keep your sanctum well stocked with the basics and can spend 1 hour in your sanctum refreshing your supplies in order to meet the requirements for Prescient Planner, even if you haven't been able to purchase goods.

    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[General's Gambit](/Feats.aspx?ID=7019) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 91

**Archetype** [Marshal](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=254)

**Prerequisites**
[Marshal Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6351); [Five-breath Vanguard Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7011)

</column>

---

You move strategically forward to draw the enemy’s attention away from your allies. You Stride toward an enemy and attempt to [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=2387), except you can use [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) or Warfare [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) instead of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38). On a success, in addition to the normal outcome for Creating a Diversion, the enemy becomes [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) with you until the start of your next turn and can’t use reactions against allies in your aura. On a critical success, the enemy becomes fascinated with you until the end of your next turn.

You've trained with weapons used by your genie ancestors. For the purpose of determining your proficiency, martial geniekin weapons are simple weapons and advanced geniekin weapons are martial weapons.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Genius Mutagen](/Feats.aspx?ID=121) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=7" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 81

</column>

---

Specialized tweaks to your formula that supplements your genius considerably broaden the benefits you gain from cognitive mutagens. When you’re affected by a [cognitive mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=87), you also gain the mutagen’s item bonus to Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, Medicine, Nature, Performance, Religion, and Survival checks. In addition, you can communicate telepathically with creatures within 60 feet with whom you share a language. The communication is two-way once you establish it, so a creature you contact can also communicate with you.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Gentle Death and Rebirth](/Feats.aspx?ID=7009) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
<trait label="Yaoguai" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=833" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 87

</column>

---

You were once born from the energies of the land and nature, and by their power, you can return to life again. Once per year, when you die, your remains become protected as if under the effects of a 5th-rank [_peaceful rest_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1625) spell. If your remains are brought and buried within 1 mile of where you were born, after a week, you return to life with the effects of a successful (but not critically successful) 9th-rank [_resurrect_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=123) ritual.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=604" />
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
<trait label="Modification" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=410" />
<trait label="Unstable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=416" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 111

**Prerequisites**
[armor innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=1)

**Access**
Tian Xia origin

**Trigger**
You would take damage.

</column>

---

Your armor has a retractable spike-covered shell reminiscent of Hwanggot’s heavily armored geobukseon, or “turtle ships.” The shell unfolds across your body, giving you a +4 circumstance bonus to AC and [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 2 to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage until the end of your next turn. Spiked chains propelled by small bursts of black powder also erupt from the shell, dealing 3d4 piercing damage plus 2 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) (basic Reflex save against your class DC) to all creatures in a 5-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387).

<traits>

You tune to the earth and stone around you, extending your senses through it in rippling waves. You gain [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) in your kinetic aura. Once per round, you can [Point Out](/Actions.aspx?ID=97) a creature you can sense with tremorsense as a free action.

---
**Level (13th)** The tremorsense becomes [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411).

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 212 **Archetype** [Geomancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=100) **Prerequisites** Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10); ability to cast spells from spell slots; at least one spell with the [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125), or [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) trait --- You feel a deep connection to the world no matter where you are, a phenomenon known as “terrain attunement.” When you expend a spell slot to cast a spell with a trait that corresponds to the type of terrain you are currently in (as listed below), you gain the terrain attunement effect for that type of terrain. The GM might determine an attunement applies as long as it's prevalent enough around you. For instance, you might be in aquatic terrain on a riverbank or on a boat. Similarly, one place might count as multiple types of terrain, such as a mountain in the far north being both arctic and mountain. In this case, you choose only one terrain attunement effect, even if the spell has traits that would apply to each terrain type. Certain terrain attunements affect your enemies instead of you. If they do, when you cast the spell you apply the listed effect to all enemies who are either adjacent to you, in the area of the spell, or targeted by the spell. These enemies receive the listed saving throw against your spell DC to attempt to avoid the effect.
  • **Aquatic** ([water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)) You ride the currents of water for 1 round. If you're in the water, you gain a swim Speed equal to your land Speed. If you're on a surface, temporary waves of water follow your movements, allowing you to use your swim Speed—if you have one—as your land Speed.
  • **Arctic** ([cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27)) Arctic rime covers your foes' bodies. Enemies must attempt a Fortitude save. They take a –5-foot status penalty to their Speeds for 2 rounds (–10-foot on a critical failure).
  • **Desert** ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)) The scorching heat of the desert dehydrates your foes. Enemies must attempt a Fortitude save. On a failure, they're [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) until they drink water or another potable liquid.
  • **Forest** ([plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125)) Branches and vines reach out to get in your foes' way. Enemies must attempt a Reflex save. On a failure, they become [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) for 1 round (clumsy 2 on a critical failure).
  • **Mountain** ([earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55)) The rugged endurance of the mountain protects you from harm. You gain resistance to physical damage (except [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374)) equal to the spell level for 1 round.
  • **Plains** ([plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125)) The growing fields and pulsing vitality of the plains provide you vigor. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to the spell level for 1 round.
  • **Sky** ([air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5)) A gust of wind carries you aloft. You can [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) up to 10 feet. If you're in the air at the end of the turn and don't have a fly Speed, you fall.
  • **Swamp** ([plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125)) Your magic draws in noxious swamp gas to fumigate your foes. Affected foes take [persistent poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) equal to half the spell's level (minimum 1 damage) with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save.
  • **Underground** ([earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55)) The endless darkness of the cavern depths opens up its secrets to your senses. For 1 round, you gain [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415) as well as imprecise [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) out to 15 feet.
**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the geomancer archetype. Geomancer Dedication leads to... [Attuned Stride](/Feats.aspx?ID=2999), [Attunement Shift](/Feats.aspx?ID=2996), [Draw from the Land](/Feats.aspx?ID=3000), [Quickened Attunement](/Feats.aspx?ID=3004), [Read the Land](/Feats.aspx?ID=3001), [Rough Terrain Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=2998), [Shared Attunement](/Feats.aspx?ID=2997), [Terrain Shield](/Feats.aspx?ID=3002)

>
[Get Behind Me!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7863) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Guardian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=859" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 45

**Prerequisites**
[Intercept Attack](/Actions.aspx?ID=3305)

</column>

---

When saving your allies from harm, you push them behind you to better protect them. When you use [Intercept Attack](/Actions.aspx?ID=3305) to protect an ally, you can move that ally up to 10 feet if they’re willing. You can’t move the ally to a position outside your reach, you can’t move them into or through obstacles, and you must move them farther away from the source of the attack if possible. This movement doesn’t trigger reactions.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Ghost Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3496) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 46

**Archetype** [Ghost](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=177)

**Prerequisites**
You died and returned as a ghost.

</column>

---

You have risen as a shell of your former self, a spirit of mist and anguish. You gain the [ghost](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=51), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=149), and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) traits, and the [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694). Your undead craving is to settle your unfinished business. You also gain the [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) trait except you can't pass through solid objects unless you select the Pass Through feat. Being a ghost has the following major effects.

 **Floating** You can float but are still tethered to the ground. Replace your land Speed with an equal fly Speed. You can't rise more than a few inches above the ground when you [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94). This means you can move above many types of difficult or hazardous terrain without moving slowly or being damaged, even though you can't fly without limit. You can [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36), [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37), and take similar actions, and use your fly Speed for any calculations that would normally require your land Speed.

 **Items** You can transmute physical items to make them part of your incorporeal form. This requires spending 10 minutes with the items within reach, during which you transform the items into part of your form; you can return items you already have incorporated to a corporeal state at the same time. The items retain all their runes and other abilities, need to be invested normally if they have the [invested](/Traits.aspx?ID=98) trait, and need to be worn, held, or stowed appropriately. Once you've incorporated the items, you and other incorporeal creatures can use them normally—you can Interact with them, Release them, and so on. Your incorporated weapons gain the benefits of the [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297) property rune, allowing you to use them normally against both corporeal and incorporeal creatures. Incorporated items become corporeal again only if you transmute them back or are destroyed, in which case, they drop to the ground under you.

 **Attacks** Your unarmed attacks become [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103) and deal negative damage instead of their normal type.

 **Strength** Unlike most incorporeal creatures, your Strength modifier is not –5; you keep the same Strength score you had before you became a ghost, though you can only attempt Strength-based skill checks—typically [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks—against other incorporeal creatures, as normal for an incorporeal creature. Against incorporeal creatures, use your Strength normally to determine the results of Athletics checks, Strikes with melee weapons, and any other checks or damage rolls dependent on Strength.

 **Ties that Bind** When you become a ghost, work with your GM to choose a bound site and unfinished business, both of which matter for your character's story, as well as some ghost archetype feats. Your bound site tethers you to the physical world and is typically either a location important to you in life or the place where you died. Unfinished business keeps you from passing to the afterlife. If someone resolves your unfinished business, you decide whether to accept the change and pass on, or to fight it. If you pass on, you get a few minutes to say your goodbyes, and then move into the River of Souls and the afterlife. Your character ceases to be. If you fight the change, you remain, though you and the GM might determine a new unfinished business. If you are physically destroyed, you cease your existence as a ghost but still might not be able to pass on to the afterlife if your unfinished business is incomplete. In this liminal state, you might come across strange energies and become another sort of creature, or anchor to a [summoner](/Classes.aspx?ID=18) and become an eidolon. 

<title level="2">Ghost Dedication leads to...</title>
[Frightful Moan](/Feats.aspx?ID=3497), [Ghost Flight](/Feats.aspx?ID=3500), [Ghostly Grasp (Ghost)](/Feats.aspx?ID=3499), [Ghostly Resistance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3498), [Headless Haunt](/Feats.aspx?ID=7699), [Pass Through](/Feats.aspx?ID=3501), [Rejuvenation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3502)

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You have focused your training on hunting and defeating ghosts, spirits, and all manner of haunts. Pick [Spirit Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or Haunt Lore; you become trained in this skill. If you were already trained in both skills, you become trained in a new Lore skill of your choice.

 Choose two cantrips from the occult spell list. Each cantrip must have the [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47), [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), or [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117) trait. You can cast these spells as innate occult spells. You gain access to the Cast a Spell activity if you didn't have it already. You're trained in occult spell attack rolls and spell DCs. You can usually replace material components with somatic components, so you don't need a spell component pouch. Your key spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the ghost hunter archetype.

<title level="2">Ghost Hunter Dedication leads to...</title>
[Ghost Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=2281), [Grave's Voice](/Feats.aspx?ID=2278), [Investigate Haunting](/Feats.aspx?ID=2279), [Peer Beyond](/Feats.aspx?ID=2282), [Spirit Spells](/Feats.aspx?ID=2280)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 114

**Archetype** [Cultivator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=278)

**Prerequisites**
[Cultivator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7085); you aren't [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517)

</column>

---

Deviating from the orthodox path, you tread an inauspicious descent littered with flowers of death; this heretical choice will, in time, earn you the enmity and fear of more traditional cultivators. You become [sanctified](/Traits.aspx?ID=519) with the [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) trait. You also learn the [_call spirit_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=112) and [_commune_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=114) rituals, which can be used to contact only [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) or entities from the Void or the [Netherworld](/Planes.aspx?ID=36).

When you cast a ritual, you can reduce the number of secondary casters by 1 as you direct decaying fragments of your own soul, felled by your proximity to death, to assist with the ritual. When you do, you must fulfill any requirements for the secondary caster, and you attempt the secondary check normally performed by that secondary caster. You can’t replace a secondary caster who’s the target of the spell (as in the [_atone_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=108) ritual).

<title level="2">Ghost-path Epiphany leads to...</title>
[The Bitter Scholar's Promotion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7093)

You shriek a death sentence upon a single target within 120 feet, forcing it to experience the final moments of your mortal life as you were dragged through a howling mob and forced to kneel before the [_final blade_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1094) that took your life and head. The target is subject to the effects of a 5th-rank [_vision of death_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1742) with a DC equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. An invisible arm extends from you to grab and manipulate objects. The arm reaches up to 15 feet, grabs an unattended object of 1 Bulk or less, and immediately deposits it in one of your free hands or at your feet. Alternatively, it reaches up to 15 feet and performs a simple Interact action like pushing open a window, though it can't perform actions that require significant mechanical dexterity. For every 5 levels you have, the amount the hand can lift increases by 1 Bulk, and the arm's range increases by 15 feet. Being ghostly, the arm can affect [ghosts](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=51), [spirits](/Traits.aspx?ID=149), and other [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) entities, though in most cases, you need an awakening for this to be useful.

The arm reaches up to 15 feet, grabs an unattended object of 1 Bulk or less, and immediately deposits it in one of your free hands or at your feet. Your control over your ghostly form grows. You gain the [advanced undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1695) and can interact with physical objects, with limits. You can attempt Strength-based skill checks against physical creatures and objects.     right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"

[Ghostly Resistance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3498) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 47

**Archetype** [Ghost](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=177)

**Prerequisites**
[Ghost Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3496)

</column>

---

Your ghostly form becomes innately weaker but also gains resistance to many forms of damage. Your maximum HP is reduced by your level. You gain resistance 1 to all damage except for [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75), [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128), and any damage done by a weapon with the [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297) rune (or any other source that acts like a _ghost touch_ rune). This resistance increases to 2 if the source is non-[magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103).

 At 10th level, the resistance increases to 2, or 4 if the source is non-magical. At 16th level, the resistance increases to 3, or 5 if the source is non-magical.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"

[Ghostly Resonance](/Feats.aspx?ID=9182) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 49

</column>

---

Your runes don’t just draw power from the world of the spirits— they can let even the most mundane objects harm spirits as well. When you etch or trace a [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) or [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) rune on a weapon or creature, you can grant it the [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) weapon property rune. For a weapon, this doesn’t count toward the weapon’s limit on property runes. For a creature, the rune applies to all unarmed Strikes the creature makes. This benefit lasts as long as the rune remains.

You fade into a slightly incorporeal form as you move. You [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to half your Speed. This movement doesn’t trigger reactions, and you can move through enemies’ spaces during it. If you have a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350), you can instead [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) up to half your fly Speed.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Electricity" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=56" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=152" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 25

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Add the following text to the Ghosts in the Storm impulse for Pathfinder Society play: "If the Strike is magical and already has the maximum number of property runes, the wielder can choose one to suppress to gain shock."_

</column>

---

Clouds, like eager pets, are drawn to you and to those in your good graces. Fast-moving gray clouds surround you, as well as your allies while they're in your kinetic aura. Anyone surrounded by these clouds gains a +2 status bonus to Reflex saves and [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks. When an affected creature uses a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) action, clouds dance around it. Until the start of its next turn, it's [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4), and its Strikes gain the [_shock_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=303) rune.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Ghoul Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3504) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 48

**Archetype** [Ghoul](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=178)

**Prerequisites**
You were killed by ghoul fever.

</column>

---

You have succumbed to ghoul fever, dying and returning as a [ghoul](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=52), an undead cursed with a never-ending hunger for dead flesh that slowly overrides your reason and willpower until you would do anything for the meal you crave. In addition to the personality changes, your body changes as well. Your ears become pointed, and your skin grows blueish and pale. Your fingernails sharpen into claws; your teeth become razor sharp, ready to tear flesh off the bone; and your tongue grows long and pointed.

 You gain the [ghoul](/Traits.aspx?ID=218) and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) traits and the [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694). Your undead craving is for the flesh of dead creatures; freshly dead corpses from sapient creatures fulfill your cravings much more than non-sapient or rotted corpses, but any dead creature can stave off the hunger for at least a little while. You gain two [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) weapon group. The first unarmed attack is a claw that deals 1d4 slashing damage with the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) and [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179) traits, and the second unarmed attack is a set of jaws that deal 1d6 piercing damage and have the finesse trait.

 You gain the Consume Flesh action. Satisfying your craving is difficult. Consuming Flesh temporarily satiates you. Many ghoul feats have extra abilities or functions that can be used when you are satiated, though using those abilities also causes you to lose your satiated status. You can always Consume Flesh, but eating more than a normal amount has no further effect; a ghoul's hunger is satiated, or it is not.

 **Consume Flesh** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Requirements** You are adjacent to the corpse of a Small or larger creature that died in the last hour; **Effect** You devour a chunk of the corpse. You become satiated for 1 hour.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the ghoul archetype

<title level="2">Ghoul Dedication leads to...</title>
[Corpse Stench](/Feats.aspx?ID=3512), [Feverish Enzymes](/Feats.aspx?ID=3507), [Flailtongue](/Feats.aspx?ID=3888), [Glutton for Flesh](/Feats.aspx?ID=3511), [Grave Strength](/Feats.aspx?ID=3508), [Replenishing Consumption](/Feats.aspx?ID=3505), [Secret Eater](/Feats.aspx?ID=3890), [Sickening Bite](/Feats.aspx?ID=3510), [Swift Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=3506), [Tunneling Claws](/Feats.aspx?ID=3891)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Giant Hunter](/Feats.aspx?ID=3900) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=136" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 23

</column>

---

You have studied [giants](/Traits.aspx?ID=79) and hunt them with efficiency. When you roll initiative and can see a giant, you can [Hunt Prey](/Actions.aspx?ID=10) as a free action, designating that enemy as your prey. 

You can use this free action even if you haven't identified the giant yet with [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26). The benefit doesn't apply against giants disguised as other creatures, and the GM determines whether it applies against a creature disguised as a giant.

<title level="2">Giant Hunter leads to...</title>
[Giant Slayer](/Feats.aspx?ID=3904), [Roll with It (Ranger)](/Feats.aspx?ID=3903)

<title level="2">Adventuring with Ekundayo</title>

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 23

Ekundayo eventually develops his own methods to pursue his favored enemies—giants. Once he gains the Magical Crafting feat at 4th level, he begins to craft specialized ammunition and runes for weapons. As long as his attitude toward the PCs is at least friendly, he shares these discoveries with them, unlocking the following ranger class feats and items as soon as his level equals the level of the feat or item.

**Related Feats**: [Giant Slayer](/Feats.aspx?ID=3904), [Hamstringing Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=3902), [Roll with It (Ranger)](/Feats.aspx?ID=3903), [The Harder They Fall (Ranger)](/Feats.aspx?ID=3901)

You can create bigger snares for quick deployment, making it more likely for a creature to walk into your snares. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 56

**Prerequisites**
You have succeeded at an important task given by a [dragon](/Traits.aspx?ID=50), such as procuring a special treasure for their hoard.

</column>

---

In pleasing the cravings of a mighty dragon, they have deigned to impart some of their magical essence into your body. Your eyes begin to glow and change color while your limbs and neck grow a veneer of scales, all the same color as the associated dragon, accompanied by a near-insatiable desire to amass a hoard of your own. You gain the [_dragon breath_](/Spells.aspx?ID=499) sorcerer bloodline spell, emulating the breath of the associated dragon, and a focus pool of 1 Focus Point. If you already have a focus pool, increase your number of Focus Points by 1. You [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) by counting and arranging your treasure.

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 41 **Usage** imbued into a body ikon --- Your blood turns a divine gold, shining in moments its spilled and begetting new life. The imbued ikon gains the following effects. **Immanence** If your divine spark remains in your body ikon for 10 continuous minutes, you regrow one damaged or ruined limb or organ.
**Transcendence—Shed the Mortal Skin** (healing, light, transcendence, vitality) Like the serpent, that most ancient of immortals, you shed your skin, revealing a glowing divine form. If you are currently taking persistent fire or acid damage, you immediately end the effect. Until the beginning of your next turn, you shed bright light in a 20 foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) like a torch. The next time you are dealt damage by an enemy before the beginning of your next turn, you shed glowing ichor in a square adjacent to you, and where it hits the earth, a glowing, thorned herb grows. A creature other than you can pluck and consume the herb with an Interact action to regain a number of Hit Points equal to half of the damage you were dealt by the attack that sprouted the herb.

When you unleash electricity from your innovation, you can bounce it off obstacles, creating a field of electric death. Even if a creature is in the area from multiple bounces, it takes the damage only once.

Your elemental lineage manifests in the polished gleam of precious metals, such as silver and gold, or even rare and valuable skymetals like [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=271) or [orichalcum](/Equipment.aspx?ID=276). This natural luster enhances your charm; you become trained in your choice of [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) or [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14). If you would automatically become trained in both these skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. If you're trained in Society, you also gain the [Courtly Graces](/Feats.aspx?ID=772) skill feat.

Your will manifests into divine weapons to protect and arm your followers. When you gain this feat, choose one type of weapon with special significance to you, such as a [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386) or a [sickle](/Weapons.aspx?ID=364). This becomes your favored weapon. You and your hierophant both treat this weapon as a simple weapon for the purposes of proficiency. You and your hierophant gain the [critical specialization](/Rules.aspx?ID=2203) effect of your favored weapon and deal an additional 1d6 spirit damage with [Strikes](/Rules.aspx?ID=2895) made with your favored weapon. If one of your current domain spells can deal a type of damage other than [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), you can choose to match this damage type (for instance, wreathing your weapon in sacred ashes that deal fire damage if you have the [fire](/Domains.aspx?ID=76) domain).

**Archetype** [Gladiator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=251)

**Prerequisites**
[Impressive Performance](/Feats.aspx?ID=5159)

</column>

---

You know how to turn combat into a form of entertainment. You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) general feat for [Gladiatorial Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41). If you were already trained in Gladiatorial Lore, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice.

 At the start of a combat encounter, if you have spectators, you gain a number of temporary HP equal to your character level for 1 minute and you can roll Performance for your initiative. If there are sapient creatures observing a combat encounter, and these onlookers are neither engaged in the combat themselves nor directly assisting any participants, the combatants have spectators. The GM is the final arbiter of whether or not a combat has spectators.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Outlaws of Alkenstar</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #180: The Smoking Gun](/Sources.aspx?ID=125) pg. 77

**Prerequisites**
You were present at the death of the [medusa](/Monsters.aspx?ID=297) Alethsia, whose vitrumantic powers were passed on to you in the wake of her destruction.

</column>

---

Even if vitrumancy is a mystery to you, your blood and flesh know the secrets of the art of arcane glass. Patches of your skin to flicker into glass without warning. By focusing the effect, you can concentrate the glass into a powerful protective layer of magical obsidian. Once per day, you can cast [_stoneskin_](/Spells.aspx?ID=312) on yourself as an innate primal spell, though the spell covers you in a layer of glass instead of stone. During this innate stoneskin, you gain the Shatter Glass reaction. At 18th level, the stoneskin is heightened to 6th level instead of 4th.

**Shatter Glass**<actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** An adjacent creature Strikes you with a melee weapon or [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack and deals damage; **Requirements** Your innate _stoneskin_ from Glass Skin is active; **Effect** You shatter some of the glass on your skin to damage your attacker. The attacker takes 3d10 damage and the duration of the _stoneskin_ decreases by 1 minute. At 14th level, the damage increases to 4d10, and at 18th level, the damage increases to 5d10.

<traits>

<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 206

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14)

</column>

---

You are adept at quickly scanning loose papers and carefully discerning the contents of sealed letters without damaging the seal. You can attempt [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) checks to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=22) on a message that is only partially glimpsed, upside down or reversed from your perspective, or even sealed. However, on a critical failure, the recipient is made aware of your efforts (for instance, you damage the seal or disturb the papers in some way). When using this feat to decipher sealed letters, your attempt to Decipher Writing gains the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) trait. This feat doesn't prevent witnesses from noticing your efforts, particularly with sealed letters which you must manipulate directly in order to read; you might need to attempt [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) or [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks to avoid being noticed.

You have developed a capacity to store more flesh within your gaunt body to leave yourself satiated longer. If you [Consume Flesh](/Feats.aspx?ID=3504) while satiated, you become fully satiated. You stay fully satiated for 3 hours, after which you become satiated for 1 hour. If you're fully satiated when an ability would end your satiation, you cease being fully satiated but remain satiated. If you have [Grave Strength](/Feats.aspx?ID=3508), you gain a +10-foot status bonus to your Speed when fully satiated instead of a +5-foot status bonus for being satiated.

You've learned to recognize the telltale writings and other signs that indicate the presence of magical traps. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to find magical traps, to AC against attacks made by magical traps, to saves against magical traps, and to checks to [Disable](/Actions.aspx?ID=69) magical traps. Even if you aren't [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519), you get a check to find magical traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap. 

You're also adept at avoiding the effects of traps that feature magical writing, such as runes, glyphs, ancient script, or other forms. When you attempt a saving throw against the effects of these traps, if you roll a success, you get a critical success instead. If you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead.

You can summon a mass of magic energy in your hand that, naturally, you use to smack those who offend you. You conjure forth a spectral bangmangi club for 1 minute, which appears in your hands, though you can give it to another creature to wield. This weapon is a _+1 striking ghost touch_ club.

At 13th level, the bangmangi is a _+2 greater striking ghost touch_ club.

**There is a more recent version of this, [click here to view.](/Feats.aspx?ID=8532)** **Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 134, [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 135 **Archetype** [Firework Technician](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=119) **Prerequisites** [Firework Technician Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3245) --- Flames and explosions sear the air in a riot of color and devastation that rivals that wrought by even the wildest goblin party. The display is both so beautiful and chaotic that, while mesmerizing, it poses a significant risk to the physical health, sight, and hearing of anyone who gets too close. You gain the Goblin Jubilee fireworks display. **Goblin Jubilee** ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Cost** 1 fireworks display; **Effect** Chaos fills a 20-foot burst within 120 feet. All creatures in the area takes 3d6 fire damage and 3d6 sonic damage and must attempt a Fortitude save. You can expend versatile vials to increase the potency of this effect; for each versatile vial you expend as part of this display, increase the fire and sonic damage by 1d6 each. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) and [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) until the end of its next turn and takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature is dazzled and deafened for 1 minute and takes full damage.
**Critical Failure** The creature is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for 1 round, dazzled and deafened for 1 minute, and takes double damage.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Godbreaker](/Feats.aspx?ID=6049) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=656" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 127

**Archetype** [Wrestler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=270) (Level 20)

**Prerequisites**
[Crushing Grab](/Feats.aspx?ID=5985); [Whirling Throw](/Feats.aspx?ID=6008)

**Requirements**
You have a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90).

</column>

---

You have mastered an ultimate grappling technique capable of breaking even the mightiest of foes. You hurl the creature 20 feet into the air, following behind it with a powerful jump, and then make an unarmed Strike. If the Strike is successful, you can repeat this process up to two more times, moving the creature an additional 20 feet directly up into the air with each Strike; the creature keeps the grabbed or restrained condition throughout the sequence. If you miss with any of the Strikes, Godbreaker and the grabbed or restrained condition immediately end and both you and the opponent fall, taking [falling damage](/Rules.aspx?ID=402) as normal for the total height of your jump.

 If all three Strikes are successful, you immediately grab the creature and bring it crashing to the ground, dealing your unarmed Strike damage plus falling damage to it. You land on your feet adjacent to the creature, you take no damage from the fall, and the creature remains grabbed or restrained by you.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs=""
>
[Godling Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7392) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 131

**Archetype** [Godling](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=293)

</column>

---

Your Calling allows you to begin walking the path to true deific ascension, inspiring followers as your divine seed grows. Your first follower is your hierophant—the high priest of your new faith—whom you rely on to spread your word and provide an anchoring mortal presence as your perspectives are increasingly pulled toward the cosmic. When you gain this feat, choose one willing ally to be your hierophant. If your hierophant is not trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC, they become trained for as long as they are your designated hierophant. If your hierophant dies or chooses to part ways with you, you can designate a new hierophant by communing with the chosen ally for a period of 24 hours. 

Your Calling allows you to seize the [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) magic typically restricted to deities. Choose one domain to claim (see list of domains [here](/Domains.aspx)). You learn the initial domain spell for this domain. You gain a pool of [Focus](/Rules.aspx?ID=285) Points with 1 Focus Point and you can Refocus by taking 10 minutes to replenish your divine energy from the planes beyond. You gain expert proficiency in spell modifier and spell DC, and your spellcasting ability for these spells is your choice of Wisdom or Charisma, decided when you gain this feat.

Your hierophant also gains the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity and can cast the domain spell you learned with Godling Dedication. When they Cast the Spell in this way, your Focus Point is expended as the cost of the spell. Your hierophant uses their own spellcasting proficiency in spell modifier and spell DC when casting a spell in this way, and they use their own Wisdom or Charisma modifier (matching your choice). If your hierophant has mythic power, they can spend a Mythic Point to cast any divine spell they gain by being your hierophant at mythic proficiency.

<title level="2">Godling Dedication leads to...</title>
[Absolve Sins](/Feats.aspx?ID=7396), [Assume Godhood](/Feats.aspx?ID=7402), [Claim Cardinal Domains](/Feats.aspx?ID=7393), [Divine Invulnerability](/Feats.aspx?ID=7394), [Font of Life or Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=7397), [Gird Champion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7398), [Heroic Weakness](/Feats.aspx?ID=8014), [Myth of Quick-Thinking](/Feats.aspx?ID=8015), [Myth of Realm-Walking](/Feats.aspx?ID=8016), [Pass Vengeful Judgement](/Feats.aspx?ID=7399), [Receive Prayers](/Feats.aspx?ID=7395), [Sanctified Relic](/Feats.aspx?ID=7400), [Stymie the Gods](/Feats.aspx?ID=7401)

Spend a Mythic Point; for the next minute, you gain a +10-foot status bonus to all your Speeds and are quickened. You can use the extra action each round to Stride, Step, or Leap.

    right="Feat 20"

>
[Golden Body](/Feats.aspx?ID=1166) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=112" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #150: Broken Promises](/Sources.aspx?ID=15) pg. 76

</column>

---

You perfect your body, refining the flex of every muscle and the bend of every joint to maximum efficiency. Your unarmed Strikes gain the [deadly d12](/Traits.aspx?ID=174) trait, and you have [fast healing 20](/Rules.aspx?ID=796), causing you to regain 20 HP at the start of each of your turns provided you have at least 1 HP.

<title level="2">Paragons of Promise</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #150: Broken Promises](/Sources.aspx?ID=15) pg. 75

The citizens of Promise represent some of the most capable experts, greatest minds, and powerful warriors on Golarion—ideal teachers and trainers for PCs who want to maximize their own potential. If the PCs secure Visitor’s Pins or an alliance with Mengkare, their access to Promise’s trainers and records unlock all of the following uncommon class feats.

**Related Feats**: [Apex Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=1160), [Aura of Unbreakable Virtue](/Feats.aspx?ID=1161), [Bloodline Metamorphosis](/Feats.aspx?ID=1162), [Efficient Alchemy (Paragon)](/Feats.aspx?ID=1163), [Emblazon Divinity](/Feats.aspx?ID=1164), [Enduring Debilitation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1165), [Song of the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=1168), [Spell Mastery](/Feats.aspx?ID=1843), [Superior Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=1170), [Ultimate Flexibility](/Feats.aspx?ID=1732), [Unstoppable Juggernaut](/Feats.aspx?ID=1631)

[Golden Dragon's Bounty](/Feats.aspx?ID=7100) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 116

**Archetype** [Familiar Sage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=279)

**Prerequisites**
[Familiar Sage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7095)

</column>

---

Your familiar alters the material of a spell into that of a precious metal. If the next action you use is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) that deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, that damage is your choice of [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916), [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2920), or steel for the purposes of weaknesses, resistances, vulnerabilities, and the like. At 14th level, [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2915) is added to the list of metal choices. The spell gains the [metal](/Traits.aspx?ID=505) trait.

<title level="2">Golden Dragon's Bounty leads to...</title>
[Seal of the Golden Dragon](/Feats.aspx?ID=7102)

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Golden Erinys Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=8930) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 109

**Archetype** [Sister of the Golden Erinys](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=380)

**Prerequisites**
[Sister of the Golden Erinys Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8929)

</column>

---

Whether you're a keen student of vengeance or you picked up techniques after being a common target for the sisters' punishment, you've learned to dig painfully into your opponent's flesh. In this stance, you can make fury's fang unarmed attacks. These deal 1d6 piercing damage; are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group; and have the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=544), [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=611), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661), and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) traits.

 While in the stance, if you critically hit with a melee Strike that deals piercing damage, the target is [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1 (with a DC to remove equal to your class DC); this is in addition to any critical specialization effect you might gain from the attack.

<title level="2">Golden Erinys Stance leads to...</title>
[Cruel Piercing](/Feats.aspx?ID=8934)

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Fists of the Ruby Phoenix</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #167: Ready? Fight!](/Sources.aspx?ID=86) pg. 76

**Archetype** [Golden League Xun](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=93)

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Underworld Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8)

</column>

---

You are a xun for the Golden League, aiding the organization. You gain expert proficiency in two of the following skills (or in two other skills of your choice in which you're trained, if you were already an expert in the listed skills): [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3), [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7), or [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15). In addition, if you use Underworld Lore to [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=23) or [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26), when you get a success, you get a critical success instead.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the Golden League Xun archetype.

<title level="2">Golden League Xun Dedication leads to...</title>
[Beneath Notice](/Feats.aspx?ID=2735), [Menacing Prowess](/Feats.aspx?ID=2736), [Rope Mastery](/Feats.aspx?ID=2737), [Silent Sting](/Feats.aspx?ID=2738)

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Golden Legionnaire Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8835) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 32

**Archetype** [Golden Legionnaire](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=373)

**Prerequisites**
trained in heavy armor

**Access**
You're invited by a current member of the Eagle Knights or the People's Council.

</column>

---

You're a wall of metal standing against the tide of Andoran's enemies. When you [Raise a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=2316), you also gain your shield's circumstance bonus to your Fortitude DC against attempts to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376), [Reposition](/Actions.aspx?ID=2379), or [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) you. You also gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) general feat for Warfare Lore. If you were already trained in Warfare Lore, you also become trained in a [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skill of your choice.

**Special** You can take this dedication even if you haven't taken more than two non-dedication feats from the [Eagle Knight archetype](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=314).

<title level="2">Golden Legionnaire Dedication leads to...</title>
[Armed and Armored](/Feats.aspx?ID=8839), [Commitment to Protection](/Feats.aspx?ID=8836), [Commitment to Valor](/Feats.aspx?ID=8840), [Commitment to Vigilance](/Feats.aspx?ID=8844), [Hell-Lancer Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=8842), [Legion's Aim](/Feats.aspx?ID=8837), [Polished Distraction](/Feats.aspx?ID=8838), [Watch Your Back](/Feats.aspx?ID=8845)

Your flesh has been specially treated with the same arcane and alchemical processes used to toughen the skin of [flesh golems](/Monsters.aspx?ID=238). Increase your maximum Hit Points by an amount equal to your level. You gain resistance to physical damage (except adamantine) equal to your number of class feats from the golem grafter archetype.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the golem grafter archetype.

You lower yourself to the ground and take an imposing, knuckle-walking stance. While in this stance, the only Strikes you can make are gorilla slam unarmed attacks. [Grand Medic's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3435) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 78

**Archetypes** [Druid](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=6), [Wizard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=12) (Level 20), [Wizard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=218) (Level 20)

**Prerequisites**
[Druid Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=701) or [Wizard Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=742)

</column>

---

Your mask is infused with restorative magic associated with Ibex, the Flourishing Field, so it constantly repairs itself. You gain [fast healing 5](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=15). If you lose a limb or other body part, it regrows within 1 day. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only one creature, you can choose to have the spell also give that creature temporary Hit Points equal to the spell's level until the start of your next turn.

<title level="2">Masks of the Magic Warriors</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 78

In becoming Jatembe's new Magic Warriors, the heroes have unlocked secrets of magical potential that none have reached since the earliest Ten Magic Warriors walked the plazas of the Magaambya.

 On reaching 20th level, the heroes should have the option of taking one of these archetype feats, based on the type of animal they chose for their mask when they first created it in _Pathfinder Adventure Path #169: Kindled Magic_. These options are each themed to one of Jatembe's magic warriors, but if a hero's mask doesn't fit with a specific animal from this list or the player feels their animal embodies a different effect from the list, feel free to reflavor the feat names to fit the hero's spirit face. For instance, the Cunning Trickster mask could easily be a rodent or a fox, not just a spider.

**Related Feats**: [Cunning Trickster Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3433), [Emancipator's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3434), [Protective Spirit Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3436), [Sky Master Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3437), [Stalking Feline Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3438), [Storyteller's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3439), [Thick Hide Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3440), [Tireless Guide's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3441), [Vigilant Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3442)

You can extend a tangle of vines or tendrils to support your arms and extend your reach. When you wield a melee weapon that requires two hands, doesn’t have reach, and deals at least 1d6 damage, you can change between a typical two-handed grip and an extended two-handed grasp using an Interact action. Weapons wielded in your extended grasp gain reach of 10 feet. This grasp is less stable and powerful than a typical grip, reducing the weapon’s damage die by 1 step.

[Grasping Spirits Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7125) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Animist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=836" />
<trait label="Apparition" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=837" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 23

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

</column>

---

Gaining substance from your magic, your apparitions increase the range of your spells, which then pull your enemy closer. If the next action you use is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) that has a range and targets one creature, increase that spell’s range by 30 feet. As is standard for increasing spell ranges, if the spell normally has a range of touch, you extend its range to 30 feet. In addition to the normal effects of the spell, your apparitions briefly take on semi-physical forms and attempt to drag the target toward you. The target must attempt a Fortitude saving throw against your spell DC; on a failure, it is pulled up to 30 feet directly toward you.

</title>

<traits>

**Archetype** [Lastwall Sentry](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=15)

**Prerequisites**
[Lastwall Sentry Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=882)

</column>

---

Your time spent hunting the undead allows you to sense them. You sense undead as a [vague sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=413) similar to a human’s sense of smell, an uncomfortable sensation akin to smelling something cloying and rotting. When in proximity to the undead, you eventually sense their presence, though you might not do so instantly, and you can’t pinpoint their location. An undead using a disguise or otherwise trying to hide its presence must attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check against your Perception DC to hide its presence from you. If the creature succeeds at its Deception check, it is then temporarily immune to your Grave Sense for 1 day.

    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Grave Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=3607) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Lastwall Sentry](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=15)

**Prerequisites**
[Lastwall Sentry Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=882); [Grave Sense](/Feats.aspx?ID=885)

</column>

---

Your ability to sense undead has improved. You sense undead as an [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) sense with a range of 60 feet: an uncomfortable sensation brushes against your spirit and stinks of rot. When in proximity to an undead, you can sense its presence, but it has the [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) condition instead of the [observed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=27) condition. An undead using a disguise or otherwise trying to hide its presence must attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) or [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check against your Perception DC to hide its presence from you. If the creature succeeds, it's [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39), and you have to use the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) basic action to detect the creature. As with hearing and other imprecise senses, you still need to Seek to locate an undetected creature.

Your time with the Knights of Lastwall has taught you the secrets of creating and improving upon Lastwall soup. Add [Lastwall soup](/Equipment.aspx?ID=516) to your list of herbal items. >

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Blood Lords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #184: The Ghouls Hunger](/Sources.aspx?ID=147) pg. 80

**Archetype** [Ghoul](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=178)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Secret Eater](/Feats.aspx?ID=3890)

**Requirements**
You are standing at the bottom of an open grave adjacent to up to four willing target creatures or objects roughly the size of a creature.

</column>

---

The maggots inhabiting your body impart you with the knowledge to travel from grave to grave, drawing upon the mystical power of the labyrinthine network of magical warrens and tunnels that connect Everglut to the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1). You can spend 10 minutes channeling this power to transport you and all target creatures or objects that are inside the grave you are standing in to a chosen grave you are aware of (unoccupied or occupied) within 100 miles. When you target an occupied or filled grave, you and all transported creatures and objects appear scattered aboveground around the targeted grave (or belowground in adjacent tunnels or passageways if available).

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Great Boaster](/Feats.aspx?ID=1071) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 75

**Archetype** [Firebrand Braggart](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=24)

**Prerequisites**
Charisma 16; [Firebrand Braggart Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1067)

</column>

---

Your bragging is particularly effective. If you succeed at a boast, you can attempt a great boast about that same skill by using your Firebrand Braggart Dedication action about the same action during the duration of your original boast’s circumstance bonus; this is an exception to the rule that you can’t make another boast about the same action until your next daily preparations. A great boast uses the Firebrand Braggart Dedication action, except that if you succeed, your circumstance bonus increases to +2 and remains for 1 hour. If you fail the great boast, you take a –2 circumstance penalty to attempt the same action for 4 hours. Once you declare a great boast about a particular action, you can’t declare a great boast about the same action until the next time you make daily preparations, regardless of whether you succeed or fail at the check. The minimum challenging task for a great boast is one with at least a hard DC for your level.

Even a single missile can throw off your enemy’s balance, and more powerful attacks leave it flustered for longer. If you hit your hunted prey with a ranged weapon, it’s off-guard until the start of your next turn. If you critically hit your prey or hit it twice on the same turn with a ranged weapon, it’s off-guard until the end of your next turn instead.

Once per day, you can use a sorcerer spell slot to cast any common [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) battle form spell of the spell slot's level as if it were a signature spell in your repertoire.

 If you have [Arcane Evolution](/Feats.aspx?ID=609), you can also choose from any battle form spell in your spellbook. If you have [Primal Evolution](/Feats.aspx?ID=613), you can Cast a Spell listed in that feat using the extra spell slot the feat grants (instead of a sorcerer spell slot).

---

Your magical blood is rich with spiritual essence, and this infusion within you allows your spells to be fully effective against incorporeal creatures, spirits, and creatures on the Ethereal Plane. Your spells have the effects of a [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297) property rune. They can target or affect a creature projecting its consciousness (such as via [_project image_](/Spells.aspx?ID=237)) or possessing another creature, even if its body is elsewhere, though you must know about the possession or projection and choose to do so. Your spells can affect creatures on the [Ethereal Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=9), though this doesn't grant you any particular ability to locate them.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 68

**Archetype** [Warrior Of Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=286)

**Frequency**

**Prerequisites**
[Hero-God's Bond](/Feats.aspx?ID=8017)

**Trigger**
Your bonded partner gains the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition or their dying value would increase.

</column>

---

A lost love. A broken [spear](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=14). Rage burning through a hero-god. When a myth speaks of a wounded partner, the hero-god often rejects the future. Too many find themselves on a battlefield, clutching a body that they swore to protect. In that moment, the wellspring of power ignites. 

Increase the value of your [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) condition by 1, to a maximum of doomed 3. You gain a +2 status bonus to attack rolls against any creature that attacked or dealt damage to your partner in the last minute. If you reduce a creature to 0 HP that attacked or damaged your partner, you gain [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) equal to twice their level. These benefits last until your bonded partner is no longer [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) or for 1 minute, whichever duration is shorter.

    right="Feat 9"

>
[Group Aid](/Feats.aspx?ID=1438) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=90" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 47

</column>

---

Your upbringing emphasized teamwork and helping your allies comes naturally to you. After you [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) an ally at a skill check that doesn't have the attack trait, you can also Aid any other ally who attempts the same skill check for the same purpose that round. You do so as a free action rather than a reaction. 

The preparation you did to help must still apply to the other allies, and you can Aid each ally only once. For example, if you helped lift up an ally to Aid them on an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to scale a wall, you could keep the same posture to give a boost to other allies attempting to scale the wall in the same round.

---

You can strong-arm people effectively, even when you don't have them isolated. When you [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394), you can compare your Intimidation check result to the Will DCs of up to five targets instead of one.

It's possible to get a different degree of success for each target. The number of targets you can Coerce in a single action increases to 10 if you're an expert, 25 if you're a master, and 50 if you're legendary.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Ardande" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=498" />
<trait label="Conrasu" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=343" />
<trait label="Ghoran" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=352" />
<trait label="Leshy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=639" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=125" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #202: Severed at the Root](/Sources.aspx?ID=242) pg. 70

**Prerequisites**
[ardande](/Traits.aspx?ID=498) or [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=668)

</column>

---

You grow a simple tool from your own body, coaxing flowers, vines, roots, and wood to grow and sprout from your flesh into the desired shape. You create a one level 0 common simple [tool](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2759) with no intricate parts or written text, such as a [crowbar](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2718), [rope](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2748), or shovel. You can’t replicate a tool kit or weapon with this ability. This item lasts for 1 minute, or until you create another tool with this ability, whichever comes first. When duration runs out, the item crumbles to mulch.

**Special** This feat gains the trait for your ancestry.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Beast Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=290)

**Prerequisites**
[Beast Lord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7345)

</column>

---

You and your united [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) have elected to become guardians of a particular location or domain. If you spend 1 week of downtime within a settlement or natural area with a 5-mile radius, you and your companion can become guardians of the area and consider it to be your guarded domain. Your guarded domain remains under your protection until you spend more than 1 month outside of your domain, after which you must spend another week of downtime to re-attune to your guarded domain. You can only have one guarded domain at a time, and selecting a new guarded domain immediately ends your protection over the previous guarded domain. 

If a creature has been in your guarded domain for at least 1 hour while you or your companion are also inside your domain, you or your companion can attempt to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391) about the target by spending 1 minute communing with the land or its residents. You attempt this check at mythic proficiency.

In addition, once per day as a 3-action activity you can spend a Mythic Point to instantly teleport yourself and your united companion to a location you are aware of within your domain. This is a [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) effect.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Nagaji" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=359" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 50

</column>

---

Your mind, like a [dark naga's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=306), foils attempts to read your thoughts. Any effect that specifically attempts to read your mind to glean information must succeed at a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check against the higher of your class DC or your spell DC to do so successfully; otherwise, it gains no information. The counteract level is equal to half your level rounded up.

>
[Guardian Ghosts](/Feats.aspx?ID=3493) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 41

**Archetype** [Undead Master](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=176)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Undead Master Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3492)

**Trigger**
You would take damage from a Strike while one of your undead companions is adjacent to you.

</column>

---

You magically divert some of the harm from an incoming attack away from yourself, forcing your undead companion to take it in your stead. Reduce the damage you take from the triggering Strike by 2 + your level. Your adjacent undead companion loses a number of Hit Points equal to the amount of damage reduced. If you have more than one adjacent undead companion, you choose which one loses Hit Points. You can't divert the damage to a temporary fragment from Their Master's Call.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Guardian Lion Roar](/Feats.aspx?ID=7078) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
<trait label="Sonic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=697" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 111

**Prerequisites**
[armor innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=1), [construct innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=2), or [weapon innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=3)

</column>

---

Your innovation is augmented with plates shaped to resemble the gaping maws of guardian lions, which you can energize to expel a stream of sonic energy reminiscent of a lion’s powerful roar. All creatures in a 20-foot line from your innovation take 2d8 sonic damage with a basic Fortitude save against your class DC. Creatures that fail this save become [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) for 1 round. The damage from this effect increases by 1d8 at 10th level and every 2 levels thereafter.

**Unstable Function** You press concealed switches in the guardian lions’ plates, extending their reach and power. Add the unstable trait to Guardian Lion Roar. The range of your roar increases to a 60-foot line. Creatures that succeed (but not critically succeed) at their save also become off-guard for 1 round. On a critical failure when attempting the flat check for this unstable action, you take sonic damage equal to your level instead of fire damage.

**Special** If your innovation is a minion, it can take this action rather than you.

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Guardian's Deflection](/Feats.aspx?ID=6147) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=825" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 165

**Trigger**
An ally within your melee reach is hit by an attack, you can see the attacker, and a +2 circumstance bonus to AC would turn the critical hit into a hit or the hit into a miss.

**Requirements**
You are wielding a single one-handed melee weapon and have your other hand or hands free.

</column>

---

You use your weapon to deflect the attack against your ally, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to their AC against the triggering attack. This turns the triggering critical hit into a hit, or the triggering hit into a miss. You gain panache until the end of your next turn.

[Guardian's Embrace](/Feats.aspx?ID=4109) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #188: They Watched the Stars](/Sources.aspx?ID=194) pg. 83

**Archetype** [Scions of Domora](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=202)

**Prerequisites**
[Scion of Domora Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=4106)

**Requirements**
You are adjacent to your spirit guide or it is sharing your space.

</column>

---

Your spirit guide discorporates to surround you in an invisible protective shroud. You gain a +2 status bonus to AC against physical attacks until the beginning of your next turn. **Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 60 **Archetype** [Guerrilla](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=327) **Prerequisites** Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48); Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) --- You're skilled in subtle tactics and using the environment against your enemies. You become trained in your choice of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50); if you are already trained in both, you become an expert in one instead. When you take this dedication, choose a single, discrete urban or wilderness location, such as “Mzali” or “the Verduran Forest”; this becomes your favored location. When you are in this location and [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96) by all enemies, you can [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405) without attempting a Stealth check as long as you move no more than half your Speed. During exploration, this also allows you to automatically approach within 15 feet of other creatures while Avoiding their Notice, as long as they aren't actively [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630) or on guard.

You can change your favored location by spending 1 week of downtime in the new location you would like to set as your favored location. Guerrilla Dedication leads to... [Battlefront Sabotage](/Feats.aspx?ID=7938), [Deathblow](/Feats.aspx?ID=7941), [Frightful Attrition](/Feats.aspx?ID=7939), [Guerrilla Weaponry](/Feats.aspx?ID=7932), [Hit and Run](/Feats.aspx?ID=7934), [Lonely Army](/Feats.aspx?ID=7940), [Rally Support](/Feats.aspx?ID=7936), [Snare Expert](/Feats.aspx?ID=7933), [Terrain Ghost](/Feats.aspx?ID=7942)

You are especially skilled in transforming simple weapons that can be easily assembled from readily available materials into deadly weapons. In your hands, a blowgun's base damage increases from 1 to a 1d4 damage die, and it gains the deadly  d4 trait. In addition, you gain the following action.  

**Guerrilla Assault** <actions string="Single Action" /> **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** You Interact to reload a sling or blowgun and then Strike. If the Strike is successful and you were undetected or unnoticed by the target when you made the attack, you are now [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) from the target after the attack, as they cannot tell  where the attack came from.

**Prerequisites**
[Chronoskimmer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3847)

</column>

---

You know the result you want and subtly nudge the timeline to your intended destination. Choose an ally or a foe. If you choose an ally, the next time within the next round that ally makes an attack roll or skill check, they roll it twice and take the higher result; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect. If you choose a foe, the next time within the next round that foe makes an attack roll or skill check, they must roll twice and take the lower result unless they succeed at a Will save against your chronoskimmer DC; this is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=110) effect. Regardless of your choice, the target becomes temporarily immune for 24 hours.

---

Using your weapon as a lever, you force your opponent to end up right where you want them. Make a Strike with the required weapon. <trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
