<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 282

**Archetype** [Mortal Herald](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=305)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Mortal Herald Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7528); Master in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39)

</column>

---

Your words speak divine truth, guiding blades and arrows to their mark. Choose an ally within 30 feet and attempt a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) check. The [DC](/Rules.aspx?ID=2629) is equal to the [hard difficulty](/Rules.aspx?ID=2630) DC of the level of your ally. On a success, the first time the targeted ally makes an attack roll before the end of their next turn, they roll the attack twice and use the better result. Regardless of the result, the target becomes immune to Guiding Words for 10 minutes.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Gunslinger Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3215) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=115" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 127

**Archetype** [Gunslinger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=114)

**Prerequisites**
Dexterity +2

</column>

---

You excel in using specific types of ranged weapons. You have familiarity with martial crossbows and firearms, treating them as simple weapons for the purposes of proficiency. You gain access to uncommon martial and simple crossbows and firearms that do not have an ancestry trait. You become trained in gunslinger class DC.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=601" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=682" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 59

**Frequency**
once per minute

**Prerequisites**
[Haft Striker Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7237)

**Requirements**
You are in Haft Striker Stance.

</column>

---

The momentum of each of your attacks feeds into the next blow in the routine, creating a brutal rhythm that enables you to give your target one continuous beatdown. [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) twice, once with your weapon and once with its haft. Each attack counts towards your multiple attack penalty, but do not increase your penalty until you have made both attacks. Then Strike twice again, once with your weapon and once with its haft.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Haft Striker Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7237) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=601" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=682" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 59

**Requirements**
You are wielding a two-handed [hammer](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=8), [spear](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=14), or [polearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=11).

</column>

---

You enter a stance that allows you to leverage the haft of your weapon to brutal effect as an effective and frighteningly efficient weapon in its own right. You treat the haft of your wielded weapon as a simple weapon dealing 1d4 bludgeoning damage. The haft is in the [club](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=5) group and has the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526) and [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602) traits. The haft shares any [fundamental runes](/Rules.aspx?ID=3167) attached to the main weapon, so long as it would normally qualify for them.

While in Haft Striker Stance, you can use feats and abilities that normally require you to be wielding two melee weapons each in a different hand, treating the haft as the second weapon, but you can’t use abilities that require you to be wielding a two-handed weapon.

<title level="2">Haft Striker Stance leads to...</title>
[Haft Beatdown](/Feats.aspx?ID=7238)

Through your heritage, you can replicate some of a hag's magic. Choose one common spell of 4th level or lower from those available to a coven, including the spells contributed to a coven by a hag of your mother's type. You can cast this spell once per day as a 4th-level occult innate spell.

 Spells available to all covens are [_augury_](/Spells.aspx?ID=15), [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=34), [_clairaudience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=39), [_clairvoyance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=40), [_dream message_](/Spells.aspx?ID=90), and [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=159).     right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hair Trigger](/Feats.aspx?ID=3205) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 118

**Prerequisites**
[initial deed](/Classes.aspx?ID=20) that allows you to Interact to draw a weapon

</column>

---

No one can react faster than you can pull your trigger. When using your initial deed, instead of [Interacting](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) to draw a weapon, you can [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) with a [firearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=16) or [crossbow](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=17) you’re already wielding. If this Strike hits, the target is also [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the end of your first turn of the encounter.

**Special** If your [initial deed](/Ways.aspx) allows you to Interact to draw a weapon more than once, this feat allows you to replace one of these Interact actions and use the other one to draw a weapon. You can't replace both Interact actions with Strikes, but you can draw a loaded firearm or crossbow with one of the actions and immediately shoot it with the other.

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 104

**Archetype** [Halcyon Speaker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=30)

**Prerequisites**
[Magaambyan Attendant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1102); member of the Magaambya of conversant rank

**Access**
A character who is Magaambyan of at least attendant rank has access to this option.

</column>

---

You devote much of your study to halcyon magic. You gain two common Halcyon cantrips and two common 1st-level halcyon spells (see [Halcyon Spells](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=30)). In addition to being able to cast your halcyon spells via your arcane or primal spell slots, you also gain a 1st-level halcyon spell slot. You can use your halcyon spell slots to spontaneously cast your halcyon spells.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the halcyon speaker archetype.

<title level="2">Halcyon Speaker Dedication leads to...</title>
[Dualistic Synergy](/Feats.aspx?ID=1116), [Halcyon Spellcasting Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=1118), [Persistent Creation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1117), [Shattered Sacrament](/Feats.aspx?ID=7742), [Speak for the Gravelands](/Feats.aspx?ID=7743)

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5); Expert in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6)

</column>

---

You are able to weave your words in such a way that you never use actual lies, but still mislead people to certain conclusions. You can attempt to make a [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) of a creature using Deception instead of Diplomacy. You can attempt to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) to a creature using [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) instead of Deception. If you fail your check to Lie, the creature realizes that you were twisting words to fool them without outright lying.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Halfling Ingenuity](/Feats.aspx?ID=1017) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Halfling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=87" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 44

**Prerequisites**
[Halfling Luck](/Feats.aspx?ID=54)

</column>

---

While your willingness to dig into a task you know little about might get you into trouble, your incredible luck often saves you from danger. You can attempt skill actions that normally require you to be trained even if you aren’t trained in that skill. If you use Halfling Luck when you fail a check for a skill with which you are untrained, you can add a proficiency bonus equal to your level, rather than 0, when you reroll the triggering skill check. You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to this rerolled skill check.

---

You've dutifully learned how to keep your balance and how to stick to the shadows where it's safe, important skills passed down through generations of halfling tradition. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) and [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15). If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

You also gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=750) general feat for Halfling [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8).

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 60

</column>

---

You favor traditional halfling weapons, so you've learned how to use them more effectively. You gain access to all uncommon weapons with the [halfling](/Traits.aspx?ID=87) trait. You have familiarity with weapons with the halfling trait plus the [sling](/Weapons.aspx?ID=72) and [shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=43)— for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.

At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.

---

The earth is both where the dead rise from and where they are put to rest. Your presence sanctifies the earth around you. When an [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) creature ends its turn within 10 feet of you, it takes 2 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage. If it’s an unholy [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creature, it takes an additional 2 vitality damage. At 10th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the spirit and [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) damage each increase by 2. Hallowed Earth lasts for 1 minute, but you can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) it.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hallowed Necromancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3459) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 24

**Archetype** [Hallowed Necromancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=172)

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13); good alignment, able to cast spells using spell slots, able to cast at least one [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117) spell

</column>

---

You've studied techniques allowing you to blend so-called hallowed necromancy into your own spellcasting to bolster the living and destroy the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). You gain the [_hallowed ground_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1103) focus spell. It costs 1 Focus Point to cast a focus spell. This feat grants a focus pool of 1 Focus Point that you can recover using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) activity. You can Refocus by meditating or praying to connect yourself to conduits of positive energy. Focus spells from the hallowed necromancer archetype have the same tradition as your spell slots.

 Casting spells that create, heal, or otherwise aid or promote undead is anathema to you, as is cooperation with undead. Using negative energy isn't anathema, as it serves a natural purpose, but twisting that negative energy for creation is blasphemous to you. If you perform acts that are anathema to your principles, you lose access to all feats from this archetype. These abilities can be regained only with an [_atone_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=2) ritual.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the hallowed necromancer archetype.

<title level="2">Hallowed Necromancer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Advanced Hallowed Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=3463), [Consecrated Aura](/Feats.aspx?ID=3465), [Death Warden](/Feats.aspx?ID=3462), [Hallowed Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=3460), [Positive Luminance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3464), [Sacred Spells](/Feats.aspx?ID=3461)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Halyard Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=9028) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=321" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 93

**Access**
You're from the Shackles

**Requirements**
A rope is within your reach, or you have a [rope](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2748) or [grappling](/Traits.aspx?ID=619) weapon in your hand.

</column>

---

You’ve learned to fight confidently while swinging from a line. You take hold of a nearby rope, throw a rope from your hand, or fire a grappling weapon at a solid surface, and then swing up to twice your Speed. You can make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) using a one-handed weapon or unarmed attack at any point during this movement. If you critically fail on this Strike, your movement ends at the point you attempted the Strike.

**Special** If you have [Pirate Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6378) and you boarded or disembarked from a boat or similar vehicle during this movement, the Strike deals one additional weapon damage die.

    right="Feat 14"

[Hammer Quake](/Feats.aspx?ID=2025) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
<trait label="Open" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=123" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 183

**Archetype** [Mauler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=68)

**Prerequisites**
[Mauler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2022)

**Requirements**
You're wielding a non-[finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179) melee weapon in two hands.

</column>

---

You smash the ground with your weapon, knocking nearby creatures to the ground. Choose a square within your reach, including your own space. If there's a foe in the chosen square, Strike that foe with the required weapon. Then attempt to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) every foe in the chosen square plus each square adjacent to that square, ignoring Trip's requirement that you have a hand free. This counts as three attacks toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after you've made the Strike, if any, and all the Trip attempts.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Hamstringing Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=3902) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=136" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 23

</column>

---

You slow your foes with a well-aimed attack. Make a Strike against your hunted prey with a –2 penalty. If you hit your prey, the creature takes a –5-foot status penalty to Speed. If you critically hit your prey, the creature takes a –10-foot status penalty to Speed. A creature immune to bleed damage does not take this penalty. The penalty can be removed using any method that removes [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) or offers a flat check to do so, such as [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=54).

<title level="2">Adventuring with Ekundayo</title>

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 23

Ekundayo eventually develops his own methods to pursue his favored enemies—giants. Once he gains the Magical Crafting feat at 4th level, he begins to craft specialized ammunition and runes for weapons. As long as his attitude toward the PCs is at least friendly, he shares these discoveries with them, unlocking the following ranger class feats and items as soon as his level equals the level of the feat or item.

**Related Feats**: [Giant Hunter](/Feats.aspx?ID=3900), [Giant Slayer](/Feats.aspx?ID=3904), [Roll with It (Ranger)](/Feats.aspx?ID=3903), [The Harder They Fall (Ranger)](/Feats.aspx?ID=3901)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hand of the Lich](/Feats.aspx?ID=3516) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 51

**Archetype** [Lich](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=179)

**Prerequisites**
[Lich Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3513)

</column>

---

Negative energy intensifies your undead form and makes your very touch the antithesis of life. You gain the [advanced undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1695). The damage die for your fist increases to 1d6 instead of 1d4, it deals negative damage instead of bludgeoning damage, and it loses the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188) trait. Your fist becomes [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103).

 When you critically hit a living creature with your fist Strike, the creature is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) until the end of your next turn unless it succeeds at a Fortitude save against your spell DC. This is a [critical specialization effect](/Rules.aspx?ID=235).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hands that Unweave Disaster](/Feats.aspx?ID=7274) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 81

**Prerequisites**
[Thief's Calling](/MythicCallings.aspx?ID=11)

</column>

---

Your hands move with uncanny sureness, dismantling danger. When you attempt an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) check to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2313), you can spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) to attempt the check at mythic proficiency. You can expend a Mythic Point when attempting to [Disable a Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=2411) to attempt the check at mythic proficiency. As normal when attempting a check with mythic proficiency, this allows you to attempt to Disable a Device even if the check normally requires expert or greater proficiency.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hardwood Armor](/Feats.aspx?ID=4283) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 34

</column>

---

Wood and bark grow over your body like armor. This hardwood armor is medium armor but uses your highest armor proficiency. The wooden armor's statistics are: _AC Bonus_ +3; _Dex Cap_ +2; _Check Penalty_ –2; _Speed Penalty_ –5 feet; _Strength_ +2; _Bulk_ 1; _Group_ [wood](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=7). Any bonuses, runes, and magical abilities of your actual armor are suppressed, but any runes that could apply to the hardwood armor are replicated onto it.

 When you use this impulse, you can also create a [wooden shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=18) in a free hand. You can [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) with this shield even if you don't have that feat. The hand wielding this shield counts as a free hand for using impulses. The shield decays in an instant if it becomes [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2) or leaves your grasp.

 The armor lasts for 10 minutes, and you can Dismiss this impulse. If you use this impulse again, any existing one ends.

---
**Level (+3)** The shield's Hardness increases by 1, its HP by 4, and its BT by 2.

    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Harmless Doll](/Feats.aspx?ID=3340) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Poppet" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=418" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 63

</column>

---

You look like nothing more than an ordinary toy, doll, or statuette, and you can fool others with your innocuous appearance. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) (or another skill if you're already trained in Deception), and you can [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) an inanimate toy or a mindless poppet. You can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) without any [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459) or [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) from creatures that don't realize you're alive, so long as you're in a location where a toy of your shape wouldn't be out of place, like a carnival booth, city street, or toy shop (at the GM's discretion). If you succeed, onlookers still see you, but they mistake you for an inanimate toy. After being fooled once, they realize you're alive, and you can't Hide from them in that way again.

fields.markdown:
May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate **Source** [Stolen Fate Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=197) pg. 13 **Archetype** [Harrower](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=204) **Access** This feat is available to all players in a Stolen Fate campaign **Requirements** You have an active harrow omen. --- You draw a card from your harrow deck just before you cast a spell to infuse your magic with its destined potential. If your next action is to Cast a Spell, the suit of the card you draw enhances the spell in one of the following ways. If the card you draw matches the suit of your active harrow omen, the effect is enhanced further as detailed below. When you Harrow Cast, attempt a DC 11 flat check. If you fail this check, you lose your active harrow omen at the end of your turn.
  • **Hammer** The force of the spell is enhanced. This effect only enhances single-target offensive spells that require you to make a successful spell attack or require a saving throw from the target to resist. If you hit the target, or if they fail their saving throw, the spell inflicts additional force damage equal to the spell's level. This additional damage doubles if your harrow omen is Hammers.
  • **Key** Some of the magic remains behind, infusing your defenses. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a +1 status bonus to your AC and all saving throws. If your harrow omen is Keys, this increases to a +2 status bonus.
  • **Shield** As the spell's magic takes effect, it heals you as well, restoring Hit Points equal to 2d6 + the spell's level. If your harrow omen is Shields, the Hit Points restored increases to 4d6 + twice the spell's level.
  • **Book** The spell's magic infuses your mind with sudden insights about the target. You can attempt to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about the target as a free action, using your spell attack roll to make the check. You gain a +2 status bonus to this roll if Books is your harrow omen.
  • **Star** The spell's magic bolsters those it aids. This effect only enhances single-target spells cast on willing subjects. The magic restores Hit Points to the affected target equal to 2d6 + the spell's level. If your harrow omen is Stars, the magic also grants the target a +2 status bonus to all saving throws until the start of your next turn.
  • **Crown** The spell's magic is hidden and subtle, and observers may not realize you're doing anything more than manipulating cards in your harrow deck. Attempt a [Fortune-Telling Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) check against all observer's Perception DCs. If your check is successful against an observer's Perception DC, that observer doesn't notice you are Casting a Spell, even though normally spells have sensory manifestations. This hides only the spell's spellcasting actions and manifestations, not its effects. If your harrow omen is Crowns, you gain a +2 status bonus to your Fortune-Telling Lore check.

fields.markdown:
May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate **Source** [Stolen Fate Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=197) pg. 13 **Archetype** [Harrower](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=204) **Access** This feat is available to all players in a Stolen Fate campaign --- You become trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11); if you are already trained in this skill, you become trained in a different skill of your choice instead. You also become trained in [Fortune-Telling Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8), and you learn the [_harrowing_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=100) ritual. In addition, once a day when you perform your daily preparations, you can perform a harrow reading for yourself if you have access to a [harrow deck](/Equipment.aspx?ID=824). Draw a card from your harrow deck—that card's suit becomes your active harrow omen for the next 24 hours and modifies several other harrower feats as detailed on the following pages. You gain the Avoid Dire Fate reaction. **Avoid Dire Fate** ([fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76)) **Requirements** you have an active harrow omen; **Trigger** you fail or critically fail a check associated with your harrow omen's suit; **Effect** Treat the failure as a success or a critical failure as a failure. You no longer have an active harrow omen. ## Associated Suit Checks
**Suit****Associated Check**
1—Hammers (Str)Strikes (both melee and ranged)
2—Keys (Dex)Reflex saving throws
3—Shields (Con)Fortitude saving throws
4—Books (Int)Skill checks

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

Choose one creature you can see, and loudly declare the creature's life forfeit by your judgment. That creature becomes your condemned foe until they are defeated, you use Harsh Judgment on a different creature, or the encounter ends. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) your condemned foe and on Intimidation checks to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) them. You have a –1 circumstance penalty to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) creatures other than your condemned foe and on Intimidation checks to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) anyone other than your condemned foe. You typically can use Harsh Judgment only during an encounter, and if you try to use it to declare someone's life forfeit during exploration or downtime, you are likely to start an encounter.

<title level="2">Harsh Judgment leads to...</title>
[Accurate Swing](/Feats.aspx?ID=3334), [Execution](/Feats.aspx?ID=3338), [Frightful Condemnation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3333)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 122

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Ghosts are not permitted for PFS play._

**Archetype** [Ghost](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=177)

**Prerequisites**
[Headless Haunt](/Feats.aspx?ID=7699)

</column>

---

Your soul bears metaphysical impressions of the innumerable other spirits imprisoned with you in the [_final blade_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1094) from which you escaped, allowing you to draw upon their memories. When you make your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), you can either gain the expert proficiency rank in one skill in which you’re untrained or raise your proficiency rank to master in one skill in which you’re trained or better. You also gain one skill feat with a minimum requirement of your new rank in the chosen skill. For the purpose of meeting level prerequisites for this feat, your level is equal to half your level.

This proficiency and feat last until you make your daily preparations again. Since the proficiency is temporary, you can’t use it as a prerequisite for any permanent character option.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Headless Haunt](/Feats.aspx?ID=7699) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 122

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Ghosts are not permitted for PFS play._

**Archetype** [Ghost](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=177)

**Prerequisites**
[Ghost Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3496)

**Access**
You were executed with a  final blade 

</column>

---

You were condemned to death and executed with one of Galt’s infamous _final blades_, where your soul was trapped for years or even decades. You might have been released alongside a host of other spirits when your prison was destroyed after the [Night of the Gray Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=99), or powerful magic or other unique circumstances might have facilitated your escape. Whatever the method, you have unfinished business preventing you from passing on to the afterlife. You gain the Remove Head action. 

**Remove Head** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** You [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) to remove your head from your ghostly body and hold it in a free hand. While your head is detached, you can use it to look around and over obstacles while remaining behind [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372), although you don’t have line of effect to target creatures unless the effect originates from your head. You can leave your head behind and move your body around independently, but your head gains the [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) condition and your body becomes [blind](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59), [deaf](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66), and unable to take any action that has the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait that requires speech or vocalization. You can cause your head to dematerialize and reappear atop your neck as a free action, which occurs automatically if it takes damage while detached or is separated from your body by more than 50 feet.

<title level="2">Headless Haunt leads to...</title>
[Fling Head](/Feats.aspx?ID=7700), [Ghostly Condemnation](/Feats.aspx?ID=7703), [Haunting Memories](/Feats.aspx?ID=7701), [Klingegeist](/Feats.aspx?ID=7702)

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />

**Requirements**

</column>

---

You attempt to finish your target with a final, well-placed shot. Make a crossbow or firearm Strike. If you've damaged the target within the last minute with the same weapon and you get a critical success on your attack roll, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or die; this is a [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) and [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93) effect. A creature that survives is temporarily immune for 1 day. Creatures with no head (such as [dullahans](/Monsters.aspx?ID=171) or [oozes](/Traits.aspx?ID=122)) are immune to this ability, and creatures with redundant heads (such as [ettins](/Monsters.aspx?ID=204)) might survive the destruction of a head.

You craft an [elixir of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=91) using [Quick Alchemy](/Actions.aspx?ID=2), and that elixir is at least 2 levels lower than your advanced alchemy level.

</column>

---

By adding a special catalyst, you transform a healing elixir into a topical projectile. You grant the elixir the [bomb](/Traits.aspx?ID=21) trait. If you throw an elixir of life bomb at a willing target, you hit even on a failure, though not on a critical failure. If your Strike with this elixir bomb hits a living target, the target regains Hit Points as if it had consumed the elixir. On a critical success, the target also gains the elixir's item bonus to saving throws against [diseases](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) and [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) for 1 minute.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Merfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=761" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 37

</column>

---

Some legends claim that the flesh of a merfolk, if consumed, can grant health, longevity, and even immortality. For obvious reasons, merfolk prefer to discourage these rumors (with violence, if necessary), but you're living proof that there's at least a fraction of truth to such claims. When [Administering First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396), [Treating Disease](/Actions.aspx?ID=2397), or [Treating Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399), you can take 1 damage to give someone a drop of your blood. When you do so, you don't need [healer's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=25), and you gain a +1 item bonus to your [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) check.

 If someone were to eat your heart and liver within an hour of your death, they would be healed of all physical injuries (regaining Hit Points up to their maximum) and would cease to age for 8 years.

Until the end of your next turn, your [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks and any [monk](/Traits.aspx?ID=112) weapons you wield deal additional electricity and sonic damage; the amount of each damage type is equal to the number of damage dice for the weapon or unarmed attack.     pfs="Standard"
>
[Heaven-Earth Encompassing Sleeves](/Feats.aspx?ID=7082) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=534" />
<trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=596" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 113

**Prerequisites**
[unfurling brocade hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=8)

</column>

---

Your magic extends to your garments. During your daily preparations, you can weave magic into a single suit of fine or high-fashioned fine clothing with long sleeves or a train, such as a robe or cloak. This clothing becomes a set of [sleeves of storage](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3110), allowing you to store items in either the sleeves or the train (you choose which during your daily preparations). This treatment also makes the clothing more durable; its [Hardness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2183) increases by an amount equal to your level, and its Hit Points increase by an amount equal to twice your level.

These benefits end if you prepare a new set of clothing, if someone else attempts to wear the clothing, or if you lose ownership of the clothing. When it ends, all items stored within the clothes fall into the nearest available space.

At 9th level, the clothing becomes greater sleeves of storage instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hedge Mage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9326) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 94

**Archetype** [Hedge Mage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=391)

**Prerequisites**
Intelligence +2 or Wisdom +2

</column>

---

[The Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26) is your laboratory and altar, and the world your workshop and study. Grounding your theoretical studies in honest labor, you work with the mundane to draw forth their hidden magic. When you take this dedication, choose [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46). You become trained in that skill, or you become expert if you were already trained. You also gain a keepsake that helps your magical studies; this keepsake is something that has perhaps been handed down to you but to which you’ve contributed a few personal touches, though it can be anything appropriate to your personal magical style. Sample keepsakes include a folio or binder of magical observations, a walking stick with mnemonic grooves, a bracelet of assorted charms and baubles, or a planchette carved into shape of a coffin. If it’s destroyed or lost, you can create a new keepsake with 1 day of downtime.

You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=3521) activity. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for hedge mage archetype spells is your choice of Intelligence or Wisdom, and they are hedge mage spells of a tradition associated with the skill chosen for this dedication ([arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) for Arcana, [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4) for Nature, [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) for Occultism, and [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) for Religion).

Your keepsake holds 4 common cantrips of your choice from your appropriate tradition. You prepare spells each day by meditating with your keepsake. You can prepare two cantrips from your keepsake each day. You can only add cantrips to your keepsake with the [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2366) activity or by other similar means.

<title level="2">Hedge Mage Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Hedge Mage Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=9327), [Community Needs](/Feats.aspx?ID=9336), [Humble Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9330), [Keepsake of Power](/Feats.aspx?ID=9334), [Peer Past the Hedge](/Feats.aspx?ID=9328), [Practical Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=9331), [Tender Ministrations](/Feats.aspx?ID=9329)

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=125" />

You sculpt a manicured maze of hedges. Up to 10 hedges spring from the ground where you choose in a 30-foot-square area within 120 feet. Each is 10 feet long, 5 feet wide, and 15 feet tall. The hedges grant standard cover, are difficult terrain, and have a Climb DC of 15. They last until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse up to 1 minute

 You can spend 10 minutes using this impulse as an [exploration](/Rules.aspx?ID=469) activity to instead create a [_cozy cabin_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1474) with hedges for walls. It lasts for 12 hours, but ends if you use the impulse again.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Fetchling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=300" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Shadow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=143" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 87

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Creatures other than the PC with the feat can store or retrieve items from the shadow; doing so is equally difficult to storing or retrieving items in a worn backpack (generally requiring Steal or a similar ability if the PC does not consent to have the item taken)._

**Prerequisites**
[Clever Shadow](/Feats.aspx?ID=2506)

</column>

---

Your shadow can contain objects. You can Interact with your shadow to store or retrieve objects, just like you would a mundane container (meaning you spend two Interact actions total to store and then retrieve the object, for example). Your shadow can contain 2 Bulk of objects, which don't count toward the Bulk you're carrying. The items remain solid but take on a shadowy patina while stored this way. Though the items are in your shadow and can be detected normally, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks to [Conceal the Objects](/Actions.aspx?ID=61) unless someone knows to check your shadow for items.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hell of 1,000,000 Needles](/Feats.aspx?ID=4265) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Metal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=505" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 31

</column>

---

The landscape fills with monumental filaments of metal. The needles lance into a cube 30 feet on a side within 500 feet. Each creature in the area takes 13d6 piercing damage, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. Each creature that fails its save is impaled, becoming [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (the DC is your class DC); a creature that critically failed is also [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) as long as it's impaled.

 The hell remains until the end of your next turn, but you can Sustain it up to 1 minute. Using this impulse again ends any previous one. The first time you Sustain it each round, lightning crisscrosses the needles. Each creature in the area takes 3d12 electricity damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. Squares in the area are [hazardous terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=454). A creature takes 6 piercing damage for every square of the area it moves through.

---
**Level (20th)** The initial damage is 17d6, and the hazardous terrain damage is 7.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 78 _[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Player characters may not be sanctified unholy._ **Archetype** [Hellbound Aspirant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=397) **Prerequisites** You do not have the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) trait. --- You’ve acquired a taste of infernal power at a very high price: When you die, your soul belongs to Hell. When you take this dedication, you are branded by your benefactor’s influence with a permanent mark. The mark usually appears on your hand and can be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) by mundane or magical means.

You gain resistance to fire equal to half your level and the Invoke Infernal Bargain action.
**Invoke Infernal Bargain** **Requirements** You are not [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67); **Effect** You call upon your infernal pact to surge with devilish power. You gain a +2 status bonus to the next attack roll, skill check, or saving throw you attempt before the end of your next turn. You then become doomed 1. **Special** You can’t retrain out of this feat unless you are able to terminate the agreement that gives you power, usually a contract with a devil. This requires a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) check against a very hard DC of your level, though the GM might set a higher DC depending on how many feats you’ve taken from this dedication. On a failure, you can’t attempt to retrain out of this feat for 1 year. On a critical failure, a clause in your contract invokes an additional penalty, usually causing you to become doomed 1 for the next year, although the GM might determine a more appropriate punishment. Hellbound Aspirant Dedication leads to... [Call Hellfire](/Feats.aspx?ID=9483), [Devil In Disguise](/Feats.aspx?ID=9481), [Devil's Wings](/Feats.aspx?ID=9487), [Dispute Terms](/Feats.aspx?ID=9485), [Fiendish Arms](/Feats.aspx?ID=9479), [Infernal Anguish](/Feats.aspx?ID=9484), [Infernal Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=9482), [The Devil Inside](/Feats.aspx?ID=9486), [Unholy Pact](/Feats.aspx?ID=9480)

</column>

---

By joining the League, you've taken on the responsibilities of a Hellbreaker. You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) general feat for both Devil Lore and Hellknight Lore. If you were already trained in one or both of those Lore skills, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice. When you roll initiative, you can attempt a Devil Lore, Hellknight Lore, or Society check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about one enemy you can see as a free action, if that skill would be applicable. The GM is the final arbiter of whether or not one of those skills would be appropriate to Recall Knowledge about the enemy.

</column>

---

Your Hellknight training teaches you to terrorize others into compliance, but you also study the structure and hierarchy of Hell. You must survive painful tests of your body and mind called reckonings, which steady your mind against all sorts of trauma. You gain resistance to mental damage equal to 1 + your number of class feats from the Hellknight Armiger archetype and other Hellknight archetypes. You become trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) and Hell [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8); if you were already trained, you become an expert instead.

**Special** You can’t select another dedication feat except dedication feats for higher positions within the Hellknights until you have gained two other feats from the Hellknight armiger archetype.

<title level="2">Hellknight Armiger Dedication leads to...</title>
[Advanced Order Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=1076), [Ardent Armiger](/Feats.aspx?ID=908), [Armiger's Mobility](/Feats.aspx?ID=911), [Diabolic Certitude](/Feats.aspx?ID=909), [Hellknight Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1078), [Hellknight Order Cross-Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=1077), [Hellknight Signifer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1082), [Mortification](/Feats.aspx?ID=910), [Order Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=1075)

You have forged your body to comply with the commands of your mind—orders steeped in the Measure and the Chain. You gain expert proficiency in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) (or in another skill in which you’re trained of your choice, if you were already an expert in Intimidation). You gain the armor specialization effects of Hellknight plate, and your resistance from that armor specialization is 1 higher than normal. In addition, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Intimidation checks while wearing your Hellknight plate.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Hellknight or [Hellknight armiger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=20) archetypes.

[Hellknight Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8812); expert in [Hellknight half plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=24) or [Hellknight plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=25)

</column>

---

You've learned how best to move in your heavy armor. When wearing heavy armor, if you meet the Strength requirement, instead of reducing the movement penalty by 5 feet, you reduce the penalty by 10 feet (typically reducing the penalty to 0). If you're a [dwarf](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=1) with the [Unburdened Iron](/Feats.aspx?ID=4393) feat, increase your Speed by 5 feet.

</title>

</traits>

**Access**

---

You gain the lesser order benefit of a Hellknight order other than the one to which you belong. This represents your time spent training with members of that order to learn their techniques and teachings. If you aren’t in good standing with a given order, you can’t receive their training.

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times, gaining the lesser order benefit from a different order each time by training with members of that order.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hellknight Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8818) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 25

**Archetype** [Hellknight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=372)

**Prerequisites**
[Hellknight Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8812); passed the Hellknight Test; trained in [Hellknight plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=25)

</column>

---

You've forged your body to be able to stand toe-to-toe with a devil, and your mind has been shaped by the strictures of the Measure and the Chain. You've become a true Hellknight. You gain expert proficiency rank in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (or in another skill in which you're trained of your choice, if you were already an expert in Intimidation). You gain the armor specialization effects of [Hellknight breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=23), [Hellknight half plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=24), and [Hellknight plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=25), and your resistance from that armor specialization is 1 higher than normal. In addition, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Intimidation checks while wearing any Hellknight armor.

**Special** You can't take both this feat and [Hellknight-Errant](/Feats.aspx?ID=8817) or [Hellknight Signifer Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8819).

<title level="2">Hellknight Preferment leads to...</title>
[Blade of Law](/Feats.aspx?ID=8824), [Hell's Armaments](/Feats.aspx?ID=8829), [Infernal Interference](/Feats.aspx?ID=8833), [March of Law](/Feats.aspx?ID=8831)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hellknight Signifer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1082) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 85

**Archetype** [Hellknight Signifer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=26)

**Prerequisites**
spellcasting class feature; [Hellknight Armiger Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=907); lawful alignment; member of a Hellknight Order; passed the Hellknight Test

</column>

---

You have bolstered your force of will with the power of the Measure and the Chain. Upon initiation, you receive a signifer mask, often devoid of eyeholes or other decorative features. The mask doesn’t obscure your vision, though it makes it impossible for others to see your eyes. While wearing your signifer’s mask, you gain +1 circumstance bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to Lie, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks, and Deception DCs against [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85). You gain expert proficiency in Intimidation (or in another skill in which you’re trained of your choice, if you were already an expert in Intimidation) as well as in your choice of [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13).

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Hellknight signifer or [Hellknight armiger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=20) archetypes.

<title level="2">Hellknight Signifer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Advanced Order Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=1076), [Gaze of Veracity](/Feats.aspx?ID=1084), [Hellknight Order Cross-Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=1077), [Masked Casting](/Feats.aspx?ID=1083), [Signifer Armor Expertise](/Feats.aspx?ID=1086), [Signifer's Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=1085)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hellknight Signifer Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8819) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 25

**Archetype** [Hellknight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=372)

**Prerequisites**
[Hellknight Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8812); passed the Hellknight Test; trained in [Hellknight breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=23); you have a spellcasting class feature.

</column>

---

You've bolstered your force of will with the power of the Measure and the Chain. You've officially joined the ranks of Hellknight signifers, and you receive a signifer's mask, often devoid of eyeholes or other decorative features. The mask doesn't obscure your vision, though it makes it impossible for others to see your eyes. While wearing your signifer's mask, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394), and Deception DCs against [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302). You gain expert proficiency rank in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (or in another skill in which you're trained of your choice, if you were already an expert in Intimidation), as well as in your choice of [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46).

**Special** You can't take both this feat and [Hellknight-Errant](/Feats.aspx?ID=8817) or [Hellknight Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8818).

<title level="2">Hellknight Signifer Preferment leads to...</title>
[Branding Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=8834), [Conjure Hell](/Feats.aspx?ID=8828), [Gaze of Veracity](/Feats.aspx?ID=8825), [Masked Casting](/Feats.aspx?ID=8821), [Signifer's Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=8826)
